B.title: Embolization of brain arteriovenous malformations with intent to cure: a systematic review.
B.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Endovascular embolization has been established as an adjuvant treatment strategy for brain arteriovenous malformations (AVMs). A growing body of literature has discussed curative embolization for select lesions. The transition of endovascular embolization from an adjunctive to a definitive treatment modality remains controversial. Here, the authors reviewed the literature to assess the lesional characteristics, technical factors, and angiographic and clinical outcomes of endovascular embolization of AVMs with intent to cure.
METHODS: Electronic databases-Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid Embase, and PubMed-were searched for studies in which there was evidence of AVMs treated using endovascular embolization with intent to cure. The primary outcomes of interest were angiographic obliteration immediately postembolization and at follow-up. The secondary outcomes of interest were complication rates. Descriptive statistics were used to calculate rates and means.
RESULTS: Fifteen studies with 597 patients and 598 AVMs treated with intent-to-cure embolization were included in this analysis. Thirty-four percent of AVMs were Spetzler-Martin grade III. Complete obliteration immediately postembolization was reported in 58.3% of AVMs that had complete treatment and in 45.8% of AVMs in the entire patient cohort. The overall clinical complication rate was 24.1%. The most common complication was hemorrhage, occurring in 9.7% of patients. Procedure-related mortality was 1.5%.
CONCLUSIONS: While endovascular embolization with intent to cure can be an option for select AVMs, the reported complication rates appear to be increased compared with those in studies in which adjunctive embolization was the goal. Given the high complication rate related to a primary embolization approach, the risks and benefits of such a treatment strategy should be discussed among a multidisciplinary team. Curative embolization of AVMs should be considered an unanticipated benefit of such therapy rather than a goal.

B.title: Modern radiosurgical and endovascular classification schemes for brain arteriovenous malformations.

B.title: A 20-year follow-up of a patient with Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome: case report.
B.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome (KTS) is a rare congenital malformation characterized by a clinical triad: capillary malformations, varicose veins, and hypertrophy of soft tissues or bones in one or more limbs. Differential diagnosis from Parkes Weber syndrome is crucial; the primary distinguishing feature is the presence of arteriovenous fistulas. KTS is progressive. Management of KTS is predominantly conservative, involving lifelong elastic compression therapy and regular courses of venotonics. This case report presents the clinical follow-up of a patient with KTS over a period of more than 20 years.
CASE PRESENTATION: A female patient with KTS presented with a congenital venous malformation of the right lower extremity, characterized by predominant deep vein hypoplasia and superficial venous varicosities, with grade III chronic venous insufficiency on the right side. She also had pelvic varicosities and superficial venous varicosities of the left lower extremity. During the reported period, the patient underwent two surgical interventions for the condition and had three deliveries.
DISCUSSION: KTS follows a progressive course characterized by unilateral varicose veins, persistent embryonic veins, anomalies of the superficial and deep venous systems, low-flow venolymphatic malformations, and hypertrophy of bone and soft tissue. Pregnancy in women with KTS is considered a high-risk condition. Management of KTS is predominantly conservative, supplemented by minimally invasive procedures if necessary.
CONCLUSION: The study supports the conclusion that open surgery for KTS can lead to recurrences. Long-term use of elastic compression therapy, combined with consistent daily walking and regular courses of venotonics, may slow disease progression.

B.title: Preservation of Non-nidal Medial Veins During Microsurgical Resection of Cerebral Arteriovenous Malformations: Technical Considerations and Early Clinical Outcomes.
B.abstract: Background The surgical management of cerebral arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) requires a meticulous balance between complete nidus eradication and the preservation of adjacent normal physiological structures. While the elimination of true malformed, nidal-draining veins is mandatory to avoid intraoperative rupture, sacrificing adjacent, non-malformed, medial cortical, and deep venous channels can cause localized venous congestion, tissue infarction, and poor functional outcomes. Objective This study analyzed the clinical, radiological, and functional outcomes of a deliberate microsurgical strategy focused on preserving critical medial venous pathways during AVM resection in an early patient series. Materials and methods A retrospective study was conducted on a consecutive series of 16 adult patients (aged >18 years) who underwent micro-neurosurgical resection of cerebral AVMs (Spetzler-Martin grades I-IV) at a single private academic institution between 2018 and 2025. Preoperative baseline features, clinical presentation (hemorrhage, seizures, focal deficits), and structural profiles were documented. Microsurgical dissection emphasized circumferential nidal isolation with strict preservation of non-nidal medial veins. Long-term functional assessment was evaluated using the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) score and the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at a minimum of six months postoperatively. Results A total of 16 patients were included in the study, of whom 10 were male (62.5%) and six were female (37.5%). Primary clinical presentations included intracranial hemorrhage in 10 patients (62.5%), seizures in eight patients (50.0%), and focal deficits in nine patients (56.3%). Complete angiographic eradication of the AVM nidus was achieved in all 16 patients. No perioperative mortality was observed. Postoperative outcome assessment demonstrated improvements or stabilization in functional capacity. Favorable neurological recovery, defined as mRS 0-2, was documented in 14 patients (87.5%), supported by increases in PROMIS physical and mental health T-scores. No delayed venous infarction or hemorrhagic transformation occurred in any patient. Conclusions In this early clinical series, prioritizing the integrity of non-malformed medial veins during cerebral AVM surgery was a safe, effective, and anatomically sound strategy. Preserving healthy venous pathways surrounding the malformation limits the incidence of secondary venous hypertension, leading to exceptional functional preservation and minimal morbidity across a range of Spetzler-Martin grades.

B.title: Updates in arteriovenous malformation management: the post-ARUBA era.
B.abstract: Brain arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are complex and heterogeneous lesions that can rupture, causing significant morbidity and mortality. While ruptured lesions are usually treated, the management of unruptured AVMs remains unclear. A Randomized trial of Unruptured Brain Arteriovenous Malformations (ARUBA) was the first trial conducted to compare the effects of medical and interventional therapy. Although it concluded that medical therapy was superior in preventing stroke and death over a follow-up period of 33 months, the findings were met with intense criticism regarding several aspects of study design, progression, and analysis/conclusion. Namely, the increased use of stand-alone embolisation relative to microsurgery in a cohort with predominantly low-grade lesions combined with a short follow-up period amplified treatment risk. Subsequently, several observational studies were conducted on ARUBA-eligible patients to investigate the safety and efficacy of microsurgery, radiosurgery, and endovascular embolisation over longer follow-up periods. These reports showed that favourable safety profiles and cure rates can be achieved with appropriate patient selection and judicious use of different treatment modalities in multidisciplinary centres. Since large prospective randomised trials on AVMs may not be feasible, it is important to make use of practice-based data beyond the flawed ARUBA study to optimise patients' lifetime outcomes.

B.title: Executive Summary of the Clinical Practice Guideline on Tinnitus Update.
B.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Tinnitus is the perception of sound without an external source. More than 50 million people in the United States have reported experiencing tinnitus, resulting in an estimated prevalence of 10% to 15% in adults. The focus of this guideline is on tinnitus that is both bothersome and persistent (lasting 6 months or longer), which often negatively affects the patient's quality of life. The target audience for the guideline is any clinician, including allied health professionals, involved in managing patients with tinnitus. The target patient population is limited to adults (18 years and older) with tinnitus that is persistent and bothersome.
PURPOSE: The purpose of this guideline is to provide and update evidence-based recommendations for clinicians managing patients with tinnitus. The target audience for this guideline is any clinician involved in managing patients with tinnitus. People with tinnitus may be evaluated by a variety of health care providers, including primary care clinicians, specialty clinicians, and allied health professionals including audiologists and clinical psychologists. The target patient population is limited to adults (18 years and older) with tinnitus that is persistent and bothersome. Most people with tinnitus have associated hearing loss, such as sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) secondary to aging (presbycusis), noise exposure (noise-induced hearing loss), or acoustic trauma. Tinnitus can also be a symptom of numerous auditory and non-auditory system disorders, ranging from middle ear diseases, such as otosclerosis and eustachian tube dysfunction, to inner ear and auditory nerve pathologies such as Ménière's disease and vestibular schwannoma. Nonauditory system disorders that can cause tinnitus include vascular anomalies, myoclonus, and intracranial hypertension. The Guideline Update Group (GUG) placed emphasis on the need for thorough clinical evaluation to identify these potentially treatable and sometimes serious disorders. However, patients with identifiable causative diagnoses other than sensorineural hearing loss are excluded from this guideline as they are excluded from nearly all randomized controlled trials of tinnitus management, making it impossible to generalize trial results to these patients. Nevertheless, clinicians should decide whether to apply the recommendations of this guideline to patients with these conditions on an individualized basis. The guideline also underscores the need to distinguish between subjective, objective, and pulsatile tinnitus to further direct patient evaluation and management. Comprehensive management of objective tinnitus and pulsatile tinnitus is not within the scope of this guideline. Pulsatile tinnitus is the perception of a rhythmic sound in the absence of an external source that may be pulse-synchronous, which is often but not always related to vascular causes, or pulse-asynchronous, which is typically associated with mechanical causes such as palatal or middle ear myoclonus.1 Further, the guideline does not apply to transient ear noise, which is the sudden perception of a tonal or ringing sound in 1 ear, lasting fewer than 5 minutes, that may be accompanied by a sense of hearing loss or aural fullness, as it does not typically require clinical management.2 The guideline also excludes patients with tinnitus related to complex auditory hallucinations or hallucinations related to psychotic or seizure disorders. This is an update to an evidence-based clinical guideline developed for the evaluation and management of tinnitus. This updated guideline provides clinicians with a logical framework to improve patient care and mitigate the personal and social effects of persistent, bothersome tinnitus. The first part of the guideline is focused on the clinical evaluation of patients with tinnitus, including the history, physical exam, and selection and timing of diagnostic testing and specialty referral to identify potential underlying treatable pathology and reduce the risk of self-harm. The remainder of the guideline is focused on the evaluation and treatment of patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus, with recommendations to evaluate and measure its effects as well as to determine the most appropriate interventions to improve symptoms and quality of life.
ACTION STATEMENTS: The Guideline Update Group made strong recommendations for the following Key Action Statements (KAS): Clinicians should distinguish patients with bothersome tinnitus from patients with nonbothersome tinnitus (KAS 2). Clinicians should inquire about risks for self-harm in a patient with bothersome tinnitus (KAS 3). Clinicians should not obtain neuroradiologic imaging in patients with tinnitus specifically to evaluate the tinnitus unless specific concerning features are present (KAS 6). The Guideline Update Group made recommendations for the following KASs: Clinicians should perform a targeted history and physical examination at the initial evaluation of a patient with tinnitus (KAS 1). Clinicians should obtain a comprehensive audiological evaluation in patients with tinnitus (KAS 5). Clinicians should educate patients with tinnitus about the natural history and effects of, and management strategies for tinnitus (KAS 7). Clinicians should recommend a hearing aid evaluation for patients with hearing difficulties and persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 8). Clinicians should refer patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus for cochlear implant evaluation when they meet audiologic criteria for referral (KAS 9). Clinicians should recommend Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) to patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 11). Clinicians or their designee should assess and document outcomes of interventions in patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 15). The Guideline Update Group made recommendations against for the following KASs: Clinicians should not routinely recommend antidepressants, anticonvulsants, anxiolytics, or intratympanic medications for a primary indication of treating persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 12). Clinicians should not recommend dietary supplements for the primary indication of persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 13). Clinicians should not recommend repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for the treatment of patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 14A). The Guideline Update Group offered options for the following KASs: Clinicians may inquire about somatosensory features in patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 4). Clinicians may recommend sound enrichment to patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 10). Clinicians may offer bimodal neuromodulation to patients with persistent, bothersome tinnitus (KAS 14B).

B.title: Delayed diagnosis of a traumatic gluteal pseudoaneurysm with arteriovenous fistula and dual arterial supply mimicking a buttock abscess after a stab wound: a case report.
B.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs), with or without associated pseudoaneurysms, are uncommon complications of penetrating vascular injuries that may cause substantial morbidity and potentially fatal complications. Evidence is largely derived from case reports and case series, with important contributions from military experience. Delayed gluteal lesions may mimic a hematoma or abscess, creating a diagnostic pitfall.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 51-year-old male presented with a one-month history of a progressively enlarging painful left buttock mass following a stab wound that had been primarily sutured at a local hospital. Initial ultrasound suggested a hematoma, and the patient was admitted with a working diagnosis of "left buttock mass." Physical examination revealed a 7 × 7 cm fluctuant mass with tenderness but without overt signs of infection. Contrast-enhanced pelvic CT demonstrated a 6.8 × 3.2 cm intensely enhancing lesion within the left gluteus maximus with prominent feeding vessels, suggestive of an arteriovenous fistula or vascular malformation. Digital subtraction angiography confirmed a left gluteal pseudoaneurysm with an associated arteriovenous fistula supplied by branches of both the inferior gluteal and internal pudendal arteries, with early venous opacification. The patient underwent successful transcatheter embolization using fibered platinum coils and a cyanoacrylate-lipiodol mixture, with complete occlusion of the fistula confirmed on completion angiography. The patient recovered uneventfully and was discharged on postoperative day 2. At three-month follow-up, the patient reported no specific discomfort, and color Doppler ultrasonography showed a marked reduction in mass size with no detectable flow within the lesion.
CONCLUSION: Penetrating buttock trauma may cause a gluteal pseudoaneurysm with an associated AVF supplied by more than one internal iliac artery branch. Contrast-enhanced CT and selective angiography are important for recognizing the vascular lesion and delineating all feeding arteries. In this patient, embolization of both the inferior gluteal and internal pudendal arterial feeders achieved complete angiographic occlusion and a favorable clinical outcome, with a markedly smaller mass and no detectable intralesional flow on color Doppler ultrasonography at three months.

B.title: Sociodemographic variation in 30-day outcomes after pediatric arteriovenous malformation resection: A national surgical quality improvement program-pediatric analysis, 2016-2024.
B.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pediatric cerebral arteriovenous malformation (AVM) care shows documented disparities in access to high-volume centers, yet it is unknown whether sociodemographic factors predict validated perioperative outcomes among children who undergo resection.
METHODS: The American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program-Pediatric identified 1558 AVM resections (Current Procedural Terminology codes 61680-61692) during 2016-2024. The primary exposure was race and ethnicity; the primary outcome was 30-day composite morbidity. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, transfer route, acuity, American Society of Anesthesiologists class, lesion location and complexity, comorbidities, hemorrhagic presentation, and operative year. Firth penalization, an E-value, causal mediation, false discovery rate (FDR) correction, and sensitivity analyses were applied. Probabilistic bias analysis addressed rupture misclassification, bounding analyses addressed unreported race, and a major-morbidity composite addressed outcome heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Composite morbidity occurred in 143 children (9.2%). Non-Hispanic (NH) Black children had higher adjusted odds than NH White children (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 2.03, 95% CI 1.17-3.50; p = 0.011); no other group differed. Adjusted morbidity probability was 14.6% versus 7.9% (risk difference +6.6 %age points). The estimate was identical under Firth penalization; the E-value was 3.17. Presentation acuity did not mediate the association (indirect-effect OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.97-1.03), and hemorrhagic presentation did not differ by race (p = 0.291). The estimate remained near 2.0 under simulated true rupture prevalences of 50-70% and strengthened for a major-morbidity composite (OR 2.12, 95% CI 1.18-3.81). B.title: Intralesional Bleomycin Injections for Vascular Malformations: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
B.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular malformations are congenital anomalies of the vascular system. Intralesional bleomycin injections are commonly used to treat vascular malformations. However, pulmonary fibrosis could potentially be a severe complication, known from systemic bleomycin therapy for malignancies. In this study, the authors investigate the effectiveness and safety of bleomycin (A2, B2, and A5) injections for vascular malformations, when possible relative to other sclerosants.
METHODS: The authors performed a PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and gray literature search for studies (1995 to the present) reporting outcome of intralesional bleomycin injections in patients with vascular malformations (n ≥ 10). Predefined outcome measures of interest were size reduction, symptom relief, quality of life, adverse events (including pulmonary fibrosis), and patient satisfaction.
RESULTS: Twenty-seven studies enrolling 1325 patients were included. Quality of evidence was generally low. Good to excellent size reduction was reported in 84 percent of lymphatic and 87 percent of venous malformations. Pulmonary fibrosis was never encountered. Meta-analysis of four studies on venous malformations treated with bleomycin versus other sclerosants showed similar size reduction (OR, 0.67; 95 percent CI, 0.24 to 1.88) but a significantly lower adverse event rate (OR, 0.1; 95 percent CI, 0.03 to 0.39) and fewer severe complications after bleomycin. Symptom relief, quality of life, and patient satisfaction were reported inadequately.
CONCLUSIONS: The authors' data suggest that bleomycin is effective in reducing the size of lymphatic and venous malformations, and leads to a lower adverse event rate and fewer severe complications than other sclerosants. The included literature does not provide evidence that pulmonary fibrosis is a complication of intralesional bleomycin injections. This study represents the "best available" evidence; however, only low- to moderate-quality studies were available.

BACKGROUND: Recommendations on the management of brain arteriovenous malformations (bAVM) with respect to pregnancy are based upon conflicting literature.

Because advice to women with bAVM may influence the management of pregnancy or bAVM with significant consequences, we believe that a retrospective multicenter, case crossover study is urgently required.

B.title: Wearable Technologies for Cancer Therapy and Monitoring: A Comprehensive Review.
B.abstract: Wearable devices have emerged as pivotal innovations in oncology, revolutionizing cancer therapy and monitoring through continuous, non-invasive physiological tracking. This comprehensive review examines the integration of advanced wearable technologies-such as electrocardiography (ECG), photoplethysmography (PPG), infrared thermometers, galvanic skin response (GSR) meters, and pulse oximeters-in detecting biomarkers associated with cancer progression and treatment efficacy. By leveraging real-time data acquisition, these devices enable early identification of conditions like chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity, evidenced by ECG-derived AI models predicting cardiomyopathy risks with 2-5-fold accuracy, and PPG-based systems detecting vascular anomalies indicative of malignancies. The incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms further enhances diagnostic precision, exemplified by AI-ECG tools that dynamically forecast cardiotoxicity 12-24 months prior to clinical onset. Additionally, wearable drug delivery mechanisms, including microneedle patches for localized chemotherapy and programmable ambulatory pumps, are explored for their capacity to optimize therapeutic outcomes while mitigating adverse effects. A systematic analysis of literature sourced from Google Scholar, PubMed, and ScienceDirect underscores the transformative potential of these technologies in fostering personalized oncology care, as demonstrated by clinical trials such as the EMBRaCE program, which reported enhanced patient recovery through continuous monitoring. Despite these advancements, challenges related to motion artifact interference, data heterogeneity, and ethical concerns regarding AI transparency necessitate resolution for widespread clinical adoption. Future trajectories highlight the convergence of multimodal sensor networks with AI-driven analytics to establish autonomous monitoring systems, thereby redefining precision oncology. This review underscores the critical role of wearable devices in advancing theranostic paradigms, advocating for their integration into mainstream oncology to improve early detection, treatment personalization, and overall patient prognoses.

B.title: Natural history and treatment of craniocervical junction dural arteriovenous fistulas.
B.abstract: Dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) located at the craniocervical junction are rare vascular malformations with distinctive features, and their natural history and the optimal treatment strategy remains unclear. B.title: Modern intraoperative imaging modalities for the vascular neurosurgeon treating intracerebral hemorrhage.

This review shares the authors' experience with each modality and discusses the advantages, potential limitations, and disadvantages of each. For effective occlusion and safe obliteration of vascular anomalies associated with ICH, vascular neurosurgeons today require a thorough understanding of the various intraoperative imaging modalities available for obtaining real-time information. Use of one or more of these modalities may improve the surgeon's confidence during the procedure, the patient's safety during surgery, and surgical outcome. The modern techniques discussed include 1) indocyanine green-based video angiography, which provides real-time information based on high-quality images showing the residual filling of vascular pathological entities and the patency of blood vessels of any size in the surgical field; and 2) intraoperative angiography, which remains the gold standard intraoperative diagnostic test in the surgical management of cerebral aneurysms and arteriovenous malformations. Microdoppler is a safe, noninvasive, and reliable technique for evaluation of hemodynamics of vessels in the surgical field, with the advantage of ease of use. Intraoperative MRI provides an effective navigation tool for cavernoma surgery, in addition to assessing the extent of resection during the procedure. Intraoperative CT scanning has the advantage of very high sensitivity to acute bleeding, thereby assisting in the confirmation of the extent of hematoma evacuation and the extent of vascular anomaly resection. Intraoperative ultrasound aids navigation and evacuation assessment during intracerebral hematoma evacuation surgeries. It supports the concept of minimally invasive surgery and has undergone extensive development in recent years, with the quality of ultrasound imaging having improved considerably. Image-guided therapy, combined with modern intraoperative imaging modalities, has changed the fundamentals of conventional vascular neurosurgery by presenting real-time visualization of both normal tissue and pathological entities. These imaging techniques are important adjuncts to the surgeon's standard surgical armamentarium. Familiarity with these imaging modalities may help the surgeon complete procedures with improved safety, efficiency, and clinical outcome.

B.title: [Intralesional pingyangmycin injection in the management of macrocystic lymphatic malformations in cervical region].
B.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the therapeutic effects of pingyangmycin injection as a primary therapy of macrocystic lymphatic malformations in cervical region.
METHODS: Thirty-six patients with macrocystic lymphatic malformations in cervical region underwent the therapy of pingyangmycin injection between 2009 and 2012 at School of Stomatology, China Medical University. Among them, 16 patients had unilateral submandibular lesions, 20 patients had lesions in anterior cervical regions. The age of patients was from 6 months to 25 years old. The concentration of the drug was 1.6 mg /mL with an addition of lidocaine. The dose and cycle of treatment were dependent on the lesions' size and patients' age. The follow-up period was 12 months to 2 years after the last treatment.
RESULTS: The total effective rate was 100%, and the curative rate was 94.4%. No serious complications were encountered.
CONCLUSIONS: Intralesional Injection of pingyangmycin provides a safe and effective treatment for macrocystic lymphatic malformations in cervical region as a primary treatment.

B.title: A randomized controlled trial to optimize indocyanine green-augmented diode laser therapy of capillary malformations.
B.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Indocyanine green (ICG)-augmented diode laser therapy (ICG + DL) represents a new treatment modality for capillary malformations (CM). However, an increase of the ICG-concentration or the use of an intense pulsed light (IPL) device as light source may further optimize treatment outcomes in CM.
OBJECTIVE: This proof-of-concept trial including 15 patients (skin type II to III) with CM evaluated the efficacy and safety of ICG-augmented diode laser therapy (808 nm) at a total dose of 4 mg/kg body weight (b.w.). Additionally, five patients with extensive CM received IPL therapy before and after ICG-administration (ICG + IPL).
METHODS: ICG was intravenously administered to 15 patients with CM at a total dose of 4 mg/kg b.w. Immediately after ICG injection, diode laser pulses with different radiant exposures (20-110 J/cm(2) ) were applied as one single treatment. Five patients with extensive CM additionally received IPL (555-950 nm) therapy. Safety and efficacy were assessed both 1 and 3 months after the single treatment by a blinded investigator and the patient. Furthermore, color of the CM was objectively measured by means of a color meter (colorStriker™, Eduard Mathai GmbH, Hannover, Germany). Treatment with the flashlamp-pumped pulsed dye laser (FPDL) and the IPL alone (five patients) served as reference treatment.
RESULTS: According to the assessment by the patients and the blinded investigator, the clearance rate was slightly better after ICG + DL therapy than after FPDL treatment (P = 0.1, P = 0.8). In one out of five patients, IPL with and without ICG injection induced poor to moderate clearance of CM and persisting erythema in another patient. The correlation between the visual assessment by the blinded investigator and the colorimetric measurements was poor.
CONCLUSION: A minority of patients with CM may benefit from ICG + DL therapy, but efficacy cannot be improved by higher ICG doses.

B.title: Imaging of primary vertebral tumors and tumor-like lesions in skeletally immature patients: a pictorial review.
B.abstract: Primary vertebral tumors and tumor-like lesions in skeletally immature patients are uncommon yet clinically consequential causes of pain, deformity, and neurological compromise. Compared with adults, pediatric lesions arise in a spine with open physes, evolving marrow composition, and substantial remodeling capacity-features that shape tumor biology and imaging appearance. This pictorial review summarizes malignant tumors, benign tumors, and tumor-like lesions of the pediatric spine, adopting a modality-first, compartment-aware approach. Useful highlights include vertebra plana in Langerhans cell histiocytosis, posterior-element bias in lesions such as osteoid osteoma/osteoblastoma, and the role of whole-body magnetic resonance imaging patterns in chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis/chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis. We also update terminology and concepts for entities such as vertebral hemangioma (venous malformation) and aneurysmal bone cyst. Throughout, we couple modality choice with pediatric anatomy and growth considerations, as well as illustrating the discussion with real-life cases from our teaching files.

B.title: Fatal tracheostomy-site hemorrhage in blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome: case report and literature review.
B.abstract: Blue Rubber Bleb Nevus Syndrome (BRBNS) is a rare congenital disorder characterized by multiple venous malformations, most frequently affecting the skin and gastrointestinal tract, but occasionally involving the central nervous system and other visceral organs. Fatal outcomes are exceedingly rare and usually result from acute hemorrhage or airway compromise. This report describes a fatal case of BRBNS in a 31-year-old woman who developed uncontrollable bleeding from vascular malformations following an emergent tracheostomy performed for anaphylaxis secondary to lidocaine administration during dental treatment. Despite aggressive resuscitative measures, the patient succumbed to hemorrhagic shock. External examination revealed bluish subcutaneous lesions in the perioral region, periorbital ecchymosis, and multiple bluish, compressible subcutaneous vascular "blebs" on the right upper extremity, extending to the right hemithorax. Internally, multiple submucosal, hemorrhagic-appearing lesions were identified on the base of the tongue, hypopharynx, larynx, and aryepiglottic folds, with additional vascular malformations in the posterior mediastinum and right temporalis muscle. Histologic examination confirmed cavernous hemangiomas at the tracheostomy site. A review of the English-language literature revealed only a small number of fatal cases associated with BRBNS. This case highlights the potential for fatal airway hemorrhage in BRBNS, particularly during emergent procedures involving the upper airway. Awareness of possible laryngeal and tracheal involvement is crucial to avoid iatrogenic complications. Comprehensive autopsy remains essential to determine the cause of death, document lesion distribution, and distinguish disease-related hemorrhage from procedural injury.

B.title: Endovascular treatment of slow-flow vascular malformations.
B.abstract: Symptomatic slow-flow vascular malformations include venous malformations and lymphatic malformations, as well as combined anomalies. Endovascular therapy, consisting mainly of intralesional sclerosant injection, is now accepted as the primary treatment for most of these lesions. Magnetic resonance imaging and ultrasonography supplement physical examination for diagnosis and assessment of the extent of malformation. Endovascular treatment is usually carried out under general anesthesia. Sclerosants for venous malformations include ethanol, 3% sodium tetradecyl sulfate, and bleomycin. Lymphatic malformations can be injected with doxycycline, bleomycin, OK-432, or other sclerosants. Complications of sclerotherapy include tissue necrosis, peripheral nerve injury, hemoglobinuria, deep vein thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism. Although most vascular malformations are not cured, the majority of patients benefit from endovascular treatment.

C.title: Bone marrow adipose tissue in cardiometabolic disease: marrow niche remodeling, inflammatory hematopoiesis, and vascular pathology.
C.abstract: Bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT) is increasingly recognized as a metabolically active, endocrine, and immunomodulatory component of the marrow niche rather than a passive fat depot. This narrative review synthesizes biological, imaging, epidemiological, and therapeutic evidence linking BMAT and marrow metabolic activation with cardiometabolic disease. BMAT arises from marrow stromal progenitors and exhibits depot-specific heterogeneity, endocrine activity, insulin responsiveness, and context-dependent expansion during aging, diabetes, obesity, menopause, osteoporosis, and chronic kidney disease. Mechanistically, experimental studies indicate that marrow adipocytes and adipocyte-lineage niche cells can influence hematopoiesis through metabolic and local signaling, whereas trained immunity is established primarily in HSPCs, myeloid progenitors, and monocyte/macrophage populations. Human MRI/MRS studies characterize BMAT quantity and composition, whereas 18F-FDG PET reflects non-BMAT-specific marrow activation associated with vascular inflammation and early atherosclerosis; direct BMAT-cardiovascular evidence remains limited. Emerging population imaging and genetic analyses support BMAT as a disease-associated phenotype, particularly for osteoporosis and fractures. Interventions affecting metabolic, inflammatory, skeletal, or marrow pathways have differing degrees of BMAT-related evidence, and none has established that modifying BMAT improves cardiovascular outcomes. This review identifies BMAT as an emerging research phenotype while emphasizing that its causal, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance to cardiovascular disease remains unresolved.

C.title: Functional characterization of grass carp OXR1 in response to GCRV infection.
C.abstract: Oxidation resistance protein 1 (OXR1) protects cells from oxidative injury in several vertebrate systems, but its role during viral infection in teleosts is unknown. We cloned and characterized grass carp OXR1 (Ctenopharyngodon idella; CiOXR1) and examined its response to grass carp reovirus (GCRV). The 959-bp CiOXR1 cDNA contains a 774-bp open reading frame encoding a 257-amino-acid TLDc-domain protein. CiOXR1 transcripts were detected in all tissues examined in healthy grass carp, with the highest basal abundance in brain, followed by heart. Following genotype II GCRV-HZ08 challenge in grass carp, CiOXR1 transcript abundance increased in brain and heart. In vitro, treatment with LPS, poly(I:C), or H2O2 increased CiOXR1 transcript abundance in grass carp ovary (GCO) cells. GFP-CiOXR1 localized mainly to the cytoplasm of GCRV-infected GCO cells. Cell-based localization and functional assays used genotype I GCRV-873, which increased DCFH-probe fluorescence. Infected cells transfected with 3HA-CiOXR1 showed lower DCFH fluorescence, lower SOD1 and SOD2 transcript abundance, and reduced accumulation of viral RNA and total-protein markers. TCID50 assays further supported inhibition of infectious-virus production by CiOXR1. Total caspase-3 and caspase-9 protein abundance, their transcript levels, and selected innate immune-response markers were also reduced, whereas no significant difference in STING transcript abundance was detected. Cas13d-mediated knockdown of CiOXR1 yielded reciprocal transcript-level changes. Together, the complementary expression and knockdown results show that CiOXR1 expression is inversely related to GCRV molecular-marker accumulation and accompanies coordinated changes in intracellular oxidation, total caspase abundance, and selected innate immune-response markers. These findings further support an antiviral role for CiOXR1 and provide a foundation for research on the prevention and control of grass carp hemorrhagic disease.

C.title: The ENL-USP7 complex regulates HIV latency through BRD4 protein stabilization.
C.abstract: HIV persistence in CD4+ T cells and brain microglia is maintained by host mechanisms that enforce viral latency. We identify ENL and the deubiquitinase USP7 as a host complex that sustains HIV latency. Pharmacologic inhibition or genetic loss of ENL reactivated latent HIV. Proteomic analyses revealed an ENL-USP7-BRD4 regulatory axis associated with latency maintenance, where USP7 maintained BRD4 protein stability. Targeted USP7 degradation using PROTAC induced latency reversal and destabilized BRD4. Chromatin immunoprecipitation studies showed that ENL was required for USP7 and BRD4 occupancy at the HIV nuc-1 region but not at the 5' long terminal repeat. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing further implicated this pathway in HIV persistence within the central nervous system. Importantly, degradation of either ENL or USP7 reactivated latent HIV in resting CD4+ T cells and brain microglia from individuals receiving antiretroviral therapy. These findings identify the ENL-USP7-BRD4 axis as a therapeutically actionable mechanism sustaining HIV latency and viral reservoirs.

C.title: CD8⁺ T Cell infiltration and spatial organization in cancer: mechanisms, barriers, and therapeutic strategies.
C.abstract: The infiltration of tumors by CD8⁺ T lymphocytes is a critical determinant of antitumor immunity and response to immunotherapy. However, the presence of tumor-specific CD8⁺ T cells does not necessarily translate into effective tumor control, as multiple biological barriers can prevent their recruitment, spatial distribution, persistence, and functional activity. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the multistep mechanisms regulating CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, from immune priming and systemic trafficking to vascular entry, intratumoral migration, and tissue residency. We discuss how alterations in chemokine networks, dysfunctional tumor vasculature, extracellular matrix remodeling, stromal barriers, and immunosuppressive signals collectively drive immune exclusion and resistance to therapy. Unlike previous reviews that have focused on individual aspects of T-cell trafficking, tumor immune contexture, or immune exclusion, we integrate these interconnected mechanisms as successive biological checkpoints and link them to therapeutic strategies aimed at overcoming specific barriers. These include restoration of antigen presentation and dendritic cell function, reprogramming of chemokine pathways, vascular normalization, stromal remodeling, innate immune activation, and induction of tertiary lymphoid structures. This integrated framework highlights why increasing CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration alone may be insufficient and supports the development of rational, sequential, and spatially guided combination strategies. Advances in spatial transcriptomics, single-cell technologies, and multiplex imaging are expected to enable personalized identification of dominant immune barriers and rational design of combination therapies. Ultimately, the goal is shifting from simply activating T cells toward engineering tumor ecosystems that support sustained CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, organization, and effector function.

C.title: Treadmill exercise impedes cognitive decline in type 2 diabetic rats by improving mitochondrial function and modulating the TGF-β/Smad-3 pathway.
C.abstract: Chronic hyperglycemia and cerebral insulin resistance are the major contributors to cognitive impairment in the ageing population. Due to the increased number of the worldwide type - 2 diabetic mellitus (T2DM) population, the prevalence of cognitive decline and dementia has also increased. It is well documented that moderate aerobic exercise dramatically improves cognitive function in individuals with diabetes. However, the impact of exercise on T2DM-associated cognitive decline modulating TGF-β/Smad-3 signalling is yet to be explored. In this study, we assessed the impact of treadmill exercise on cognitive health in a preclinical model of T2DM, focusing on neuroinflammation, mitochondrial function, and the TGF-β/Smad-3 signalling pathway. To develop an experimental type - 2 diabetic model, rats were fed a high-fat diet (HFD), followed by an intraperitoneal injection of a single low dose of streptozotocin (STZ, 35 mg/kg). After confirmation of diabetes, rats underwent moderate-intensity treadmill exercise for 14 weeks. We observed a significant alternation in behavioural patterns in diabetic rats compared to controls, which reversed on exercise treatment. Moreover, chronic Type - 2 diabetes compromises mitochondrial function and increases inflammation in the hippocampal region of the brain. An increase in pro-inflammatory cytokines, such as IL-1β and TNF-α, was observed in the hippocampus of T2DM animals and was reduced by exercise. Oxidative stress is markedly increased in the type - 2 diabetic brain, resulting in compromised mitochondrial function with elevated hippocampal MDA and decreased GSH and ATP levels, which are reversed in the exercise group. Furthermore, we evaluated the role of exercise on TGF-β/Smad-3 signalling in the type - 2 diabetic brain. Exercise suppresses the overexpression of this signalling cascade in the diabetic brain. In summary, moderate-intensity treadmill exercise ameliorated type - 2 diabetes-associated cognitive impairment by decreasing oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction and downregulating the TGF-β/Smad-3 signalling pathway.

C.title: Biomarker-guided immunotherapies for primary CNS tumors.
C.abstract: Refined immunotherapeutic modalities for the treatment of primary central nervous system (CNS) tumors - vaccines, virotherapies, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and cell therapies - are starting to show efficacy in selected patients with primary CNS tumors. Still most patients do not derive a meaningful clinical benefit, despite evidence of biological activity. While the unique immunosuppressive environment of the CNS, cellular heterogeneity and brain borders prohibiting access present substantial challenges for effective treatment, there is a need to define robust biomarkers for response to immunotherapies. As immunotherapies critically depend on multiple tumor intrinsic as well as host factors, this task is substantially more challenging than defining biomarkers for response to targeted therapies. Recent advances in biomarker identification and characterization for immunotherapies have opened new avenues for precision immunotherapy approaches. This review examines the current state of biomarker-guided immunotherapy for primary CNS tumors, focusing on key biomarkers including immunogenic antigens, HLA ligandomics, tumor immune microenvironment characteristics, cell-free DNA, tumor mutational burden, and T cell populations in tumor tissue, blood, and cerebrospinal fluid. We discuss how these biomarkers can guide the selection and optimization of immunotherapeutic strategies including cancer vaccines, T cell therapy, and immune checkpoint inhibitors particularly for glioblastoma, and highlight current challenges and future directions in the field.

C.title: USP11 Drives Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Via Promoting Ferroptosis by Deubiquitinating and Stabilizing ASK1.
C.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) represents a pivotal pathological mechanism underlying ischemic cerebrovascular disorders including cerebral stroke. Currently, there are lack of effective preventive or therapeutic methods. Ubiquitin-specific protease 11 (USP11) is a member of the most prevalent ubiquitination-specific protease (USP) family. It has been shown that USP11 plays diverse and significant roles in a variety of diseases, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, prostate cancer, and intervertebral disc degeneration. However, its precise function and molecular mechanisms involvement in CIRI remain unknown.
METHODS: USP11 knockout (USP11-KO) and adeno-associated virus 9-mediated USP11 over-expression (USP11-OE) mice were established as a mouse model of CIRI, and USP11 knockdown and overexpression adenovirus were used to establish a cell model, to investigate the effect of USP11 on CIRI in vivo and in vitro. Molecular biological studies were used to clarify the mechanism of USP11 mediated ferroptosis during CIRI.
RESULTS: The expression of USP11 is increased during CIRI. Functionally, USP11 deficiency attenuated neurological deficits, cerebral infarction, neuroinflammation, and ferroptosis during CIRI, whereas specific overexpression of USP11 exacerbated these pathological processes. Furthermore, USP11 knockdown inhibited neuronal injury, inflammatory response and ferroptosis, while USP11 overexpression promoted these processes. Mechanistically, USP11 bind to ASK1 and inhibit its K48-linked ubiquitination, thereby enhancing the activity of the ASK1-JNK/p38 signaling pathway. More importantly, the regulation of USP11 on neuronal ferroptosis and CIRI relied on its regulation of the ASK1-JNK/p38 signaling axis.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study clarified the new functions and mechanisms of USP11 during CIRI. Targeting USP11-ASK1-JNK/p38-ferroptosis may be a new promising strategy for the prevention and treatment of CIRI.

C.title: Jue Tone Music Therapy for Post-stroke Depression in China: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
C.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the effects of Jue tone music therapy on depressive symptoms, sleep quality, activities of daily living, and selected serum biomarkers in patients with post-stroke depression (PSD).MethodsIn this randomized controlled trial, patients with PSD were randomly assigned to a control group or an intervention group. The control group received usual care, including sertraline hydrochloride and comprehensive rehabilitation training. The intervention group received additional Jue tone music therapy based on Five Element Music Therapy for 6 weeks. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the 24-item Hamilton Depression Scale (HAMD-24) and the depression subscale of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS-D). Sleep quality and activities of daily living were evaluated using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and the Barthel Index (BI). Serum interleukin-6 (IL-6), brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), and 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) levels were measured before and after the intervention.ResultsA total of 91 patients completed the study (control group, n = 46; intervention group, n = 45). After 6 weeks, the intervention group showed significantly lower HAMD-24, HADS-D, and PSQI scores and higher BI scores compared with the control group (all P < 0.01). Serum IL-6 levels were significantly reduced, while BDNF and 5-HT levels were significantly increased in the intervention group (all P < 0.05). No significant differences in adverse events were observed between groups.ConclusionJue tone music therapy is a safe and effective adjunct to usual care, improving depressive symptoms, sleep quality, and functional outcomes in patients with PSD.

C.title: Acute trazodone treatment ameliorates behavioral abnormalities and improves subsequent short-term memory in a lipopolysaccharide-induced mouse model of acute brain dysfunction.
C.abstract:
AIM: Systemic inflammation-associated acute brain dysfunction, typified by delirium, is linked to later cognitive impairment. Although trazodone is used clinically for delirium-related symptoms, its effects on subsequent cognition remain unclear. We examined whether acute-phase trazodone treatment influences behavioral abnormalities, later cognitive outcomes, and inflammatory/glial-related changes in an lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced mouse model.
METHODS: Adult male C57BL/6J mice received saline or LPS (3.0 mg/kg, intraperitoneally). Control mice received saline, whereas LPS-treated mice subsequently received saline or trazodone (10 mg/kg, subcutaneously). In addition to a group receiving trazodone during the acute phase (Days 0-2), a group receiving trazodone for 7 days was also included. Behavioral assessments were performed on Day 1 (acute phase), Day 3 (recovery phase), and Day 7 (postrecovery phase) using nesting, open-field, Y-maze, and novel object recognition tests. Plasma cytokines and inflammatory and glial markers in the cerebral cortex and hippocampus were also assessed.
RESULTS: During the acute phase, trazodone-treated LPS mice showed reduced locomotor activity, whereas stimulus-dependent exploratory behavior and nesting were relatively preserved. During the recovery phase, novel object recognition performance was better in trazodone-treated than in saline-treated LPS mice. Elevations of cortical Iba1 and IL-6 and hippocampal GFAP during the acute phase were evident in saline-treated LPS mice but not clearly in trazodone-treated LPS mice. Direct comparison between the two trazodone regimens showed no clear additional benefit of continued treatment.
CONCLUSION: In this model, acute-phase trazodone treatment was associated with milder acute behavioral abnormalities and better subsequent short-term-memory performance, whereas the benefit of continued treatment remained uncertain.

C.title: Macrophage fate decisions during AKI-CKD transition insights from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics.
C.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is an established risk factor for chronic kidney disease (CKD), but the cellular events that determine recovery or maladaptive repair remain incompletely defined. Macrophages are central regulators of this transition because their functional states change with time and tissue context. Recent single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic studies show that renal macrophages cannot be adequately described by a simple M1/M2 scheme. Instead, inflammatory, cycling, reparative and profibrotic programs emerge in a model- and niche-dependent manner. Experimental studies identify early S100A8/A9-associated inflammatory macrophages, cycling states and repair-associated programs involving TREM2, MRC1/IGF1 and efferocytosis. Together, these changes define a transient reparative phase in which inflammation can resolve and tubular repair can proceed. Failure to sustain this phase is associated with persistent inflammation, fibro-inflammatory niches, CD38-high and scar-associated macrophages, and progression towards fibrosis. Spatial transcriptomics further shows that interactions with injured tubular cells, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, immune cells and platelets shape macrophage function. Although the timing and dominant populations differ across experimental models, several pathway-level programs recur. Human datasets support selected inflammatory and fibrotic macrophage states but show limited one-to-one conservation of cell subsets across species. Clinical translation will therefore require conserved macrophage programs, treatment windows and biomarkers that distinguish reparative from maladaptive responses.

C.title: Anti-inflammatory Effect of Electroconvulsive Therapy and Association Between Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor Increases and Nonrelapse: A Prospective One-Year Follow-up Study.
C.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is effective for severe psychiatric disorders, but relapse after a successful acute course of ECT remains common. Identification of biological predictors of relapse is therefore clinically important. In this exploratory prospective study, we investigated changes in inflammatory and neurogenesis-related biomarkers following an acute course of ECT, and examined their association with relapse during 1-year follow-up.
METHODS: Enrolled were 30 patients with major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, or schizophrenia spectrum disorders who received their first acute course of bitemporal ECT. Clinical assessments and venous blood sampling were conducted before and after the ECT course. We measured serum inflammatory markers, anti-inflammatory factors, and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF). Relapse was prospectively evaluated using monthly Clinical Global Impression-Severity assessments over 1 year. Repeated-measures analyses were performed to examine biomarker changes and their interaction with relapse status.
RESULTS: Following the acute ECT course, 48.1% of patients achieved remission, and 37.0% experienced relapse during 1-year follow-up. ECT was associated with a significant decrease in serum soluble interleukin-2 receptor levels and significant increases in eicosapentaenoic acid and docosahexaenoic acid, indicating an anti-inflammatory effect. Notably, serum BDNF levels increased in the nonrelapse group but decreased in the relapse group, with a significant time-by-relapse interaction.
CONCLUSION: An acute course of ECT is associated with anti-inflammatory biological changes and differential modulation of serum BDNF. Increases in BDNF after ECT may be linked to a reduced risk of relapse, suggesting that serum BDNF could be a potential prognostic biomarker for long-term outcomes following ECT.

C.title: EPA restores neuroimmune homeostasis in Schizophrenia: evidence for the involvement of autophagy.
C.abstract: Immune dysregulation, particularly inflammation, may contribute significantly to the pathophysiology of schizophrenia (SZ). Autophagy is an essential cellular process that maintains neuroimmune homeostasis, but its relationship with inflammation in SZ remains unclear. Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), an omega (n)-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA), was reported to exert therapeutic effects by modulating inflammation. Here, we hypothesized that EPA alleviates SZ-related behavioral and neurochemical abnormalities via autophagy regulation. Transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood from SZ patients revealed reduced autophagic markers (BECLIN1, LC3B), which were negatively correlated with symptom severity, while P62 levels were increased, which was positively correlated with symptoms severity. SZ patients also showed an altered n-3 PUFA profile (reduced EPA and DHA, while elevated n-6/n-3 ratio). In a mouse model of SZ induced by maternal immune activation, lower Beclin1, an autophagic marker, was observed in the brains of mice. EPA treatment ameliorated SZ-like behaviors, upregulated Beclin1 expression, rebalanced glial activation toward anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective states. EPA also suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α), increased IL-10 and decreased DA/5-HT ratio in the prefrontal cortex and restored the n-6/n-3 PUFA ratio. Notably, EPA effects were largely blocked by co-administration of an autophagy inhibitor 3-methyladenine (3-MA), whereas these effects were recovered following treatment with the autophagic activator rapamycin. EPA supplementation also increased brain DHA levels, suggesting that downstream DHA-related mechanisms may additionally contribute to the observed effects. Together, these findings indicate that autophagic impairment is associated with neuroimmune and neurochemical abnormalities in SZ and support the autophagic function involved in EPA therapeutic effects on SZ-like changes.

C.title: Long-term antibiotics treatment-induced anxiety-like behavior is associated with disrupted colonic tryptophan metabolism.
C.abstract: The widespread and often excessive use of antibiotics has raised concerns about its long-term impact on host health. Growing evidence suggests that antibiotics-induced gut microbiota dysbiosis may contribute to neuropsychiatric conditions, including anxiety. However, the mechanistic pathways linking chronic antibiotic exposure, microbial disruption, and anxiety-like behaviors remain largely unclear. To investigate the effects of antibiotic exposure on gut-brain axis function, mice were administered antibiotic-containing drinking water for either short-term or long-term durations. Behavioral assessments, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, biochemical analyses, histological staining, and Western blotting were used to evaluate anxiety-like behaviors, microbiota composition, tryptophan (Trp) metabolism, intestinal barrier integrity, and inflammation in both the colon and hippocampus. Long-term, but not short-term, antibiotic treatment induced pronounced anxiety-like behaviors in mice. Microbiota analysis revealed that long-term antibiotic exposure significantly reduced microbial diversity and altered the abundance of key bacterial genera. These changes were associated with disrupted colonic Trp metabolism, reflected by decreased Trp and 5-HT levels in the colon and serum, along with suppressed expression of the Trp metabolic enzyme TPH1 and 5-HT4R. Additionally, long-term antibiotic treatment impaired intestinal barrier integrity, downregulated tight junction proteins and MUC2, and activated colonic TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammatory signaling pathways. Neuroinflammation was also observed in the hippocampus. Our results reveal a time-dependent effect of antibiotic-induced anxiety-like behaviors and suggest that gut microbiota dysbiosis, disrupted colonic Trp metabolism, intestinal barrier dysfunction, and neuroinflammation may collectively contribute to the behavioral alterations associated with long-term antibiotic exposure. These findings provide new insights into the gut-brain mechanisms underlying microbiota-associated mood disorders.

C.title: CXCR4 targeting by TPCA‑1 attenuates neuroinflammation in intracerebral hemorrhage through inhibiting NF‑κB and AP‑1 activation.
C.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH)-induced secondary brain injury (SBI) is a critical contributor to poor neurological outcomes. In this study, we aimed to identify potential small‑molecule therapeutic agents and systematically validate their neuroprotective efficacy. Bioinformatics analysis was performed to screen ICH‑related hub genes, and Connectivity Map (CMap) was used to predict candidate compounds, followed by molecular docking to verify their binding affinity. The therapeutic effect of TPCA‑1 was further evaluated in a mouse ICH model using neurological scoring, cerebral edema assessment, qPCR, Western blot, and ELISA. Bioinformatics analysis indicated that the chemokine signaling pathway is critically involved in ICH pathogenesis. Molecular docking revealed that TPCA‑1 displayed the strongest binding affinity for CXCR4 among all predicted compounds. In vivo, 20 mg/kg TPCA‑1 significantly ameliorated neurological deficits and reduced cerebral edema in ICH mice. Mechanistically, TPCA-1 interacted with CXCR4, as supported by molecular docking, MST, and CETSA assays, and suppressed downstream inflammatory signaling involving NF-κB and AP-1, thereby decreasing the production of pro‑inflammatory cytokines including TNF‑α, IL‑1β, and IL‑6. Importantly, Co-treatment with the CXCR4 inhibitor AMD3100 did not produce additional inhibitory effects. Collectively, TPCA‑1 exerts neuroprotective effects against ICH‑induced SBI by targeting CXCR4, which further inhibits the activation of NF‑κB and AP‑1 and ultimately alleviates neuroinflammation.

C.title: Endothelial fluid shear stress sensing in vascular health and disease.
C.abstract: Endothelial cells transduce the frictional force from blood flow (fluid shear stress) into biochemical signals that regulate gene expression and cell behavior via specialized mechanisms and pathways. These pathways shape the vascular system during development and during postnatal and adult life to optimize flow to tissues. The same pathways also contribute to atherosclerosis and vascular malformations. This Review covers recent advances in basic mechanisms of flow signaling and the involvement of these mechanisms in vascular physiology, remodeling, and these diseases. We propose that flow sensing pathways that govern normal morphogenesis can contribute to disease under pathological conditions or can be altered to induce disease. Viewing atherosclerosis and vascular malformations as instances of pathological morphogenesis provides a unifying perspective that may aid in developing new therapies.

C.title: Nonconventional Use of Flash-Lamp Pulsed-Dye Laser in Dermatology.
C.abstract: Flash-lamp pulsed-dye laser (FPDL) is a nonablative technology, typically used in vascular malformation therapy due to its specificity for hemoglobin. FPDL treatments were performed in a large group of patients with persistent and/or recalcitrant different dermatological lesions with cutaneous microvessel involvement. In particular, 149 patients (73 males and 76 females) were treated. They were affected by the following dermatological disorders: angiokeratoma circumscriptum, genital and extragenital viral warts, striae rubrae, basal cell carcinoma, Kaposi's sarcoma, angiolymphoid hyperplasia, and Jessner-Kanof disease. They all underwent various laser sessions. 89 patients (59.7%) achieved excellent clearance, 32 patients (21.4%) achieved good-moderate clearance, 19 patients (12.7%) obtained slight clearance, and 9 subjects (6.1%) had low or no removal of their lesion. In all cases, FPDL was found to be a safe and effective treatment for the abovementioned dermatological lesions in which skin microvessels play a role in pathogenesis or development. Further and single-indication studies, however, are required to assess a standardized and reproducible method for applying this technology to "off-label" indications.

C.title: Mimic of Peritoneal Carcinomatosis: Protein-Losing Enteropathy Revealing HRAS-Driven Generalized Lymphatic Anomaly.
C.abstract: Complex lymphatic anomalies can present with a protein-losing enteropathy. A 25-year-old woman presented with steatorrhea, weight loss, anasarca, and hypoalbuminemia. She was started on a low-fat diet, sirolimus, and trametinib monotherapy with modest symptomatic response. However, she continued to have severe malnutrition. Alternating therapy of sirolimus and trametinib is ongoing. This is the first reported case of protein-losing enteropathy as the presenting manifestation of an HRAS-driven generalized lymphatic anomaly.

C.title: Focal malformations of cortical development: new vistas for molecular pathogenesis.
C.abstract: Focal malformations of cortical development (FMCD) are highly associated with several neurological disorders including intractable epilepsy and neurocognitive disabilities. Over the past decade, several FMCD subtypes have been linked to hyperactivation of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling cascade. In view of the roles that mTOR plays in cell proliferation, size, motility, and stem cell phenotype, many of the features of FMCD such as cytomegaly, disorganized lamination, and expression of stem cell markers can be explained by enhanced mTOR signaling. FMCD result from several distinct and fascinating molecular mechanisms including biallelic gene inactivation, somatic mutation, and potentially, viral infection. These mechanisms have been directly linked to mTOR activation. Perhaps most compelling, pharmacological inhibition of mTOR has been implemented successfully in clinical trials for select FMCD and provides a new vista for treatment.

C.title: Photobiomodulation: multifaceted therapeutic effects on disorders in the central nervous system.
C.abstract: Conventional pharmacological interventions for brain diseases are often limited by complex pathophysiological mechanisms, suboptimal efficacy, and pronounced side effects. In contrast, photobiomodulation (PBM) has attracted increasing attention due to its non-invasive nature, multi-target effects, and favourable safety profile. In brain diseases, PBM employs specific light wavelengths to activate mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase and photosensitive proteins and to regulate neuronal oscillatory activity and neuroglial functions. Human studies demonstrated the efficacy of PBM in improving cognitive performance, motor symptoms, and emotional distress in patients with neurodegenerative diseases, brain trauma, and psychiatric disorders. Therapeutic outcomes are influenced by key parameters of the protocol, such as wavelength, dosage, and frequency, as well as inter-individual variability in anatomical and physiological factors. Future research needs to focus on establishing a database of disease-specific parameters to enable personalised treatment protocols by integrating imaging and molecular biomarkers and performing large-scale clinical trials to validate long-term safety and translational potential.

C.title: Functional Heterogeneity of the Autism Spectrum Disorder-Associated Gut Microbial Ecosystem Revealed by Fecal Lipopolysaccharides and Bacterial Proteomic Profiling.
C.abstract: The etiology of pediatric autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has been increasingly linked to alterations in the gut-brain axis, highlighting the intricate bidirectional communication between gut microbiota and central nervous system. The molecular mechanisms of this communication are poorly understood. Here we investigated whether ASD-associated gut microbiota could exhibit altered inflammatory molecular outputs by integrating chemistry-driven profiling of fecal lipopolysaccharides (LPS), functional bacterial proteomics, and neuroimmune cellular assays. Structural analyses revealed that LPS from non-autistic healthy donors (NASD) displayed highly conserved carbohydrate and lipid A signatures dominated by hypo-acylated mono-phosphorylated species typically associated with immunomodulatory Bacteroides-derived LPS. In contrast, LPS from ASD children exhibited increased structural heterogeneity. These molecular alterations were functionally reflected in human HMC3 microglial cells, where ASD-derived fecal LPS induced stronger IL-6 and IL-8 release compared with NASD-derived LPS, indicating enhanced neuroinflammatory potential. Functional proteomic profiling disclosed broadly comparable microbial compositions but marked metabolic divergence. These findings suggest that gut microbiota in ASD children are associated with a functionally heterogeneous microbial ecosystem characterized by altered immunostimulatory molecular outputs despite the absence of massive taxonomic shifts, with potential relevance for neuroimmune dysregulation.

C.title: A rare case of ultrastructurally proven toxoplasmic myositis masquerading as necrotizing myopathy with emphasis on pathobiology.
C.abstract: Toxoplasmosis is a zoonotic infection caused by the obligate protozoan Toxoplasma gondii. In an immunocompetent human host, the parasite forms bradyzoites (tissue cysts), mainly in skeletal muscle, eye, brain, or cardiac muscle, and remains latent. Once cysts are established, type 1 cytokine-based immunity controls the conversion to tachyzoites from bradyzoites. We propose that short-term immunosuppression can only cause a transient defect in this cycle of conversion control. The temporary lapse in conversion control releases few tachyzoites, and the host immunity in response gives rise to cytokines that can cause polymyositis. Myositis and the presence of a parasite in the muscle biopsy are very rare, even in immunosuppressed patients. We present a case of a young man with quadriplegia after immunosuppression for dengue-associated hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. We report a rare case of toxoplasmic myositis in a patient masquerading as necrotizing myopathy, with emphasis on the possible pathomechanism of myositis and ultrastructure of toxoplasma. We recommend that toxoplasma myositis should be included among the differentials of sudden muscular weakness, especially in an immunocompromised host. Our case highlights the crucial role of muscle biopsy in the diagnosis of toxoplasmic myositis. For early diagnosis, a systematic search for toxoplasmosis should be formulated in case of polymyositis, especially in immunocompromised patients, as a quicker identification of the parasite is possible and treatment response is also better in the early, acute phase of toxoplasmic myositis.

C.title: Stage-Specific Patterns of Imaging and Non-Motor Biomarkers in Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 3.
C.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Advancements in disease-modifying therapies for spinocerebellar ataxia Type 3 (SCA3) underscore the need for robust biomarkers to monitor disease progression and evaluate treatment efficacy. Although motor phenotypes have been well characterized, less is known about non-motor and imaging-based features across different disease stages. This study aimed to characterize stage-specific patterns of non-motor and imaging biomarkers in SCA3.
METHODS: This cross-observational study included 229 patients with SCA3 and 104 age- and sex-matched healthy controls from the Organization for Southeast China for cerebellar ataxia research. Non-motor symptoms were assessed using a battery of neuropsychological tests. Brain volume loss was assessed by 3.0-Tesla MRI with regions-of-interest (ROI)-based volumetric analysis. Neuroinflammation was quantified in vivo using translocator protein positron emission tomography (TSPO-PET) with the 18F-DPA-714 radioligand. Additive regression models were fitted to evaluate the cross-sectional associations between biomarkers and disease stages. Receiver operating curve (ROC) analyses were applied to estimate the discriminative ability of the candidate biomarkers.
RESULTS: Non-motor symptoms, including cognitive functions, anxiety, fatigue, depression, and sleep quality, declined after ataxia onset in SCA3. Volume loss in the brainstem and ventral diencephalon diverged from normal controls at 0.7 and 0.2 years before ataxia onset, respectively. Correspondingly, the TSPO signal in the brainstem and ventral diencephalon increased and deviated from normal throughout the disease course.
INTERPRETATION: Our findings propose a staging model of SCA3 that includes a biomarker stage characterized by multidimensional objective indicators of neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation from pre-ataxia to ataxia onset.

C.title: Highly potent, brain-penetrant EP2 receptor antagonists for the treatment of permanent focal cerebral ischaemia in male and female mice.
C.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Cerebral ischaemia is a leading cause of death in older adults and imposes a substantial global economic burden. Recent studies indicate that inhibiting the Gαs-coupled EP2 receptor reduces ischaemic brain injury by modulating neuroinflammation. However, these findings derive from the transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) model, which represents only a small subset of large-vessel occlusion (LVO) cases with successful recanalisation.
EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: We characterised the pharmacokinetic parameters of selective EP2 antagonists CJ-18, CJ-19 and CJ-21 that we recently developed. We evaluated their therapeutic efficacy in mice subjected to permanent MCAO (pMCAO), a model that more accurately reflects the majority of LVO cases, and assessed the impact of EP2 inhibition on brain injury and inflammation. Finally, we examined the effects of EP2 inhibition in neuron-glia mixed cultures exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) without reoxygenation.
KEY RESULTS: After systemic administration in mice, new compounds exhibited favourable plasma half-lives and brain penetration. In the pMCAO model, treatment with EP2 antagonists significantly reduced brain infarction in both male and female mice, in a dose-dependent manner, whilst improving sensorimotor performance without affecting muscle strength. These benefits were accompanied by reduced neuronal death, lowered pro-inflammatory cytokines and attenuated reactive gliosis within the ischaemic penumbra. In addition, EP2 inhibition by CJ-18 conferred marked neuroprotection in neuron-glia co-cultures exposed to prolonged OGD, preserving neurite integrity and postsynaptic density.
CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: This proof-of-concept study supports our drug-like EP2 receptor antagonists, particularly CJ-18, as potential treatments for permanent focal cerebral ischaemia.

C.title: [Effect of electroacupuncture on microglial activation in the spinal dorsal horn of rats with postherpetic neuralgia based on the BDNF/TrkB pathway].
C.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To observe the effects of electroacupuncture (EA) on the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)/tyrosine kinase receptor B (TrkB) pathway and microglial activation in the spinal dorsal horn of rats with postherpetic neuralgia (PHN).
METHODS: Five of 20 male SD rats were randomly assigned to the normal control (NC) group, and the remaining rats received intraperitoneal injection of resiniferatoxin solution (200 μg/kg) to establish a PHN model. Successfully modeled rats were randomly divided into a PHN group, an EA group, and an EA+BDNF group, with 5 rats in each group. The rats in the EA group received EA at ashi points, "Xinshu" (BL15), and "Danshu" (BL19) on the left side, with disperse-dense wave (2 Hz/15 Hz) and a current intensity of 1 mA, 30 min per session, once daily for 4 consecutive weeks. In the EA+BDNF group, 10 μg of recombinant rat BDNF protein solution was administered by intrathecal injection before each EA treatment. The mechanical withdrawal threshold was assessed using Von Frey analgesia meter, and the thermal withdrawal latency was evaluated using plantar thermal stimulation apparatus. Immunofluorescence staining was used to detect the positive expression of ionized calcium-binding adaptor molecule 1 (Iba-1), a marker of microglial activation, in the spinal dorsal horn. ELISA was used to measure interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) levels in the spinal dorsal horn. Western blot was used to detect the protein expression of BDNF and TrkB in the spinal dorsal horn.
RESULTS: Compared with the NC group, the PHN group showed decreased mechanical withdrawal threshold and increased thermal withdrawal latency (P<0.05), while positive Iba-1 expression, IL-1β and TNF-α levels, and BDNF and TrkB protein expression in the spinal dorsal horn were increased (P<0.05). Compared with the PHN group, the EA group showed increased mechanical withdrawal threshold and decreased thermal withdrawal latency (P<0.05), while positive Iba-1 expression, IL-1β and TNF-α levels, and BDNF and TrkB protein expression in the spinal dorsal horn were decreased (P<0.05). Compared with the EA+BDNF group, the EA group showed increased mechanical withdrawal threshold and decreased thermal withdrawal latency (P<0.05), while positive Iba-1 expression, IL-1β and TNF-α levels, and BDNF and TrkB protein expression in the spinal dorsal horn were all decreased (P<0.05).
CONCLUSION: EA could alleviate pain symptoms in rats with PHN, possibly by regulating the BDNF/TrkB pathway, inhibiting microglial activation in the spinal dorsal horn, and reducing inflammatory factor levels.

C.title: Adhesive cationic hyaluronic acid loading with small extracellular vesicles from IL-6 activated mesenchymal stem cells improves repair of corrosive esophageal injury.
C.abstract: The treatment of corrosive esophageal injury (CEI) remains challenging due to recurrent courses, frequent complications, and severe tissue damage. Enhancing the therapeutic potential of mesenchymal stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) through cytokine preconditioning has emerged as a promising strategy. In this study, functionally enhanced sEVs (E-sEVs) were generated by pretreating umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells with interleukin-6 (IL-6). E-sEVs exhibited superior capabilities in promoting fibroblast migration and suppressing macrophage-mediated inflammation compared to naïve sEVs. To improve local retention and therapeutic efficacy, E-sEVs were integrated into a cationic hyaluronic acid (CHA) hydrogel with strong bioadhesive properties, forming a composite system termed E-sEVs@CHA. In vitro assays demonstrated that E-sEVs@CHA effectively promoted endothelial cell invasion, exhibited antioxidant activity, and modulated macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. In a rat model of CEI, E-sEVs@CHA significantly reduced esophageal inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibrotic remodeling, leading to improved tissue repair and reduced stricture formation. This study presents a novel cell-free therapeutic strategy with translational potential for the management of corrosive esophageal injury.
