C.title: Vascular and lymphatic dysregulation via non-EndoMT Col2a1 signaling in bisphosphonate-related osteonecrosis of the jaw.
C.abstract: Bisphosphonate-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (BRONJ) is a severe complication of antiresorptive therapy with poorly understood vascular mechanisms. Here, we integrate whole-organ tissue-clearing imaging, single-cell transcriptomics, and proteomics to construct a multimodal atlas of the mouse and human BRONJ mandibular microenvironment. We identify gross vascular and lymphatic rarefaction and four endothelial subtypes with aberrant Col2a1 upregulation. Fibroblasts and macrophages emerge as key endothelial interactors, highlighting dysregulation of the endothelium-matrix-immune axis. Unlike homeostatic Dmp1⁺/Tfap2a⁺ fibroblasts and Stab1⁺ macrophages, BRONJ lesions feature pathological Lrrc15⁺/Chad⁺ fibroblasts and Il6⁺ macrophages, driving ectopic chondrogenesis and inflammation. Mechanistically, the COL2A1-CD44 axis (EC-to-fibroblast/macrophage signaling) and COL2A1-SDC4 axis (EC-to-fibroblast signaling) are upregulated in BRONJ disease condition, while lineage tracing excludes EndoMT, implicating extracellular matrix remodeling. We functionally validate this axis via localized Col2a1 siRNA silencing and endothelial-specific genetic deletion. Cross-species validation in human mandibles confirms vascular-lymphatic dysregulation, inflammation, and chondrogenesis. Overall, we establish vascular and lymphatic dysregulation as a BRONJ hallmark and identify the COL2A1-CD44/SDC4 axis as a therapeutic target.

C.title: Endothelial cell-microglia crosstalk mediates heart failure-associated synaptic loss and cognitive impairment in male mice.
C.abstract: Cognitive impairment affects 30%-80% of patients with heart failure, yet the mechanisms beyond reduced brain blood flow remain poorly defined. Here we show that circulating factors released during heart failure trigger senescence of brain blood-vessel endothelial cells, which in turn drives synaptic loss and cognitive decline through crosstalk between endothelial cells and microglia, the brain's immune cells. Using a pressure-overload model (transverse aortic constriction) combined with plasma transfer in 8-month-old male mice, we found that elevated circulating TGFβ2 acts on endothelial TGFBR2 and induces the secreted protein SPARC via a non-canonical MEK/ERK-MYC pathway. Endothelial SPARC then activates microglial TLR4, promoting neuroinflammation and abnormal engulfment of synapses. Endothelial deletion of Tgfbr2 or Sparc, and microglial deletion of Tlr4, each preserved synapses and improved cognition, and pharmacological Tlr4 inhibition was protective. These findings define an endothelial-microglia signaling axis and a potential therapeutic target in heart failure-associated cognitive impairment.

C.title: AI-guided discovery of a brain-penetrant LILRB4 inhibitor active in microglial and 5xFAD models of Alzheimer's disease.
C.abstract: The inhibitory microglial receptor LILRB4 (ILT3) suppresses amyloid-β (Aβ) clearance in Alzheimer's disease (AD) through ApoE-dependent signaling. Here, we report an independent artificial intelligence-guided approach for discovering small-molecule inhibitors of the LILRB4-ApoE interaction. Ultralarge-scale screening of approximately 500 million compounds identified chemically distinct molecules that bind LILRB4 with nanomolar affinity and inhibit ApoE engagement, as validated using orthogonal biophysical and biochemical assays. Structural modeling and mutational analysis defined an interdomain pocket and key residues associated with ligand recognition. In human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia, compound 4 reduced SHP1/2 phosphorylation, attenuated NF-κB activation and IL-1β secretion, and restored Aβ uptake without compromising cell viability. The compound exhibited oral bioavailability and brain penetration. In male and female 5xFAD mice, once-daily oral administration improved Y-maze performance and reduced regional Aβ42 levels, inflammatory cytokines, and CD86-positive microglia. These findings establish retrieval-based artificial intelligence as a complementary route to LILRB4 ligand discovery and identify compound 4 as a pharmacologically differentiated candidate for further optimization.

C.title: Chronic THC exposure modulates behavioral outcomes and endocannabinoid signaling in HIV-1 Tg26 mice in a sex-dependent manner.
C.abstract: While combined antiretroviral therapy (cART) has transitioned HIV-1 into a manageable chronic condition, it fails to eradicate latent viral reservoirs in the central nervous system (CNS) that drive persistent neuroinflammation and synaptodendritic injury. Consequently, people living with human immunodeficiency virus type-1 (HIV-1) often utilize cannabis to manage neurological symptoms, yet the long-term impact of exogenous cannabinoids on the HIV-1-burdened brain remains poorly understood. In this study, we utilized the HIV-1 Tg26 mouse model to evaluate how chronic Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC, 3 mg/kg) exposure influences motor coordination, thermal nociception, and endocannabinoid (eCB) signaling in the context of constitutive viral protein expression. Our results demonstrate that HIV-1 viral protein expression was associated with impaired acquisition of cerebellum-dependent motor learning in a sex-dependent manner. This deficit was primarily driven by females and coincided with elevated monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL) expression in the female cerebellum. Conversely, males exhibit increased cerebellar CB1R and CB2R expression, which paralleled preserved rotarod performance. In the spinal cord, viral protein expression was associated with thermal hyposensitivity and a reduction in 2-AG and cannabinoid receptor levels, a pattern consistent with HIV-1-associated alterations in sensory processing circuits. While chronic THC failed to produce detectable antinociceptive effects, consistent with spinal CB1R downregulation, it successfully attenuated the temporal decline of motor coordination with upregulating cerebellar CB1R. Data from a separate acute THC cohort demonstrated detectable THC and metabolite concentrations in plasma and cortex, while also revealing sex- and genotype-dependent differences in these measures. Together, these findings identify sex-specific eCB signaling as a critical factor associated with the neurobiological response to HIV-1 proteins and provide a biological framework for understanding sex-dependent variability in cannabinoid efficacy.

C.title: Device-Free Auricular Acupressure for Rosacea: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
C.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation is effective for rosacea. However, its neuroimmunomodulatory effects lack sham-controlled serum biochemical evidence, and specialized device reliance limits its clinical popularization.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of device-free auricular acupressure for rosacea and verify its neuroimmunomodulatory effects using serum biomarkers and immediate vascular imaging in a sham-controlled trial.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This single-center, randomized, sham-controlled, assessor-masked trial was conducted in the Dermatology Outpatient Department of the Second Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University from October 2025 to May 2026 and included 204 patients with rosacea who were receiving standard first-line treatment. Participants were assigned in a 1:1 ratio using block randomization. Data analysis was initiated in May 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: The active acupressure group received a Vaccaria segetalis seed on the bilateral cavum conchae (innervated by the auricular vagus branch), while the sham group received a seed on the auricular tubercle superior margin (pure somatosensory innervation). Participants performed acupressure 3 times daily for 30 seconds, with extra pressing allowed during acute flare-ups. The intervention lasted 8 weeks. Serum levels of cathelicidin antimicrobial peptide (LL-37), calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α), and interleukin (IL) 6 were measured at baseline and week 8. Multispectral imaging was performed at baseline and week 4 to assess immediate vascular responses.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was treatment success, defined as an Investigator Global Assessment (IGA) score of 0 or 1 at week 8. The number needed to treat was calculated from absolute risk difference.
RESULTS: The 204 participants were equally divided into 2 groups (102 each; active acupressure: mean [SD] age, 32.51 [10.60] years, 86 female individuals [84.3%]; sham acupressure: mean [SD] age, 30.82 [9.32] years, 86 female individuals [84.3%]). At week 8, the active acupressure group had a higher IGA success rate (58 [56.9%] vs 36 [35.3%]; relative risk, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.18-2.20; P = .003; number needed to treat, 5). Serum LL-37, CGRP, TNF-α, and IL-6 levels decreased more significantly in the active acupressure group. The immediate vascular improvement rate was 59.3% vs 7.4% (P < .001). At week 20, the active acupressure group maintained significantly lower IGA and Clinical Erythema Assessment scores. No serious adverse events occurred.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This randomized clinical trial found that device-free, on-demand intervention yielded substantial additional clinical benefits when combined with standard first-line therapy and established early sham-controlled, serum-based evidence for its neuroimmunomodulatory mechanism, potentially offering a strategy for self-management of rosacea.

C.title: Melatonin Exerts Neuroprotective Effects in Escherichia coli/Lipopolysaccharide Induced Neuronal Injury via Regulating TFRC-Related Ferroptosis.
C.abstract: Neonatal bacterial meningitis (NBM) is a severe neonatal infectious disease associated with a high incidence of neurological sequelae. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and inflammatory cytokines aggravate cerebral injury, whereas the mechanism of ferroptosis in the pathogenesis of NBM remains unclear. Melatonin (MT), an endogenous neurohormone, provides anti-ferroptotic neuroprotection in models of cerebral injury; however, its mechanism of action against NBM-related injury through ferroptosis has not been clarified. This study investigated the protective effects mediated by MT in vivo and in vitro. Rat models of LPS-induced inflammatory brain injury were established through intracerebroventricular (i.c.v.) injection, and Escherichia coli (E. coli)-infected cell models were developed to investigate the neuroprotective effects of MT against TFRC-related ferroptosis. CCK-8 assays, Western blotting, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), iron detection, and immunofluorescence, BODIPY staining were used to assess cell viability, inflammatory factors, mitochondrial ultrastructure, iron accumulation, and GPX4 expression. E. coli infection induced typical ferroptotic mitochondrial damage. MT alleviated neuroinflammation and reduced the expression of ferroptosis-related proteins both in vitro and in vivo. MT treatment increased mitochondrial GPX4 expression. The ferroptosis agonist RSL3 reversed the neuroprotective effects of MT. MT inhibited TFRC-related ferroptosis and alleviated neuronal damage. MT protects against E. coli/Lipopolysaccharide induced neuronal injury by regulating TFRC-related ferroptosis, indicating that MT may be a promising therapeutic agent for NBM.

C.title: Hijacking Developmental Immunity: Inflammation and Immune Dysregulation in Pediatric Brain Tumors.
C.abstract: Pediatric brain tumors (PBTs) remain a leading cause of cancer-related mortality in children, underscoring the need for more effective therapeutic strategies. These tumors arise from disrupted neurodevelopmental programs and evolve within a developmentally constrained immune landscape that is tolerogenic, epigenetically plastic, and susceptible to tumor-mediated co-option. Increasing evidence indicates that, besides molecular heterogeneity, the tumor immune microenvironment critically influences clinical outcomes. Despite its therapeutic promise, immunotherapy has yet to demonstrate consistent clinical benefit in most PBTs, highlighting the need for rational multimodal strategies guided by deeper understanding of tumor-immune interactions in the developing brain. To provide a comprehensive perspective on fetal immune ontogeny and its tumor-driven dysregulation we used medulloblastoma, pediatric gliomas, atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumors, and ependymoma as representative entities. Drawing on insights from developmental neurobiology, tumor immunology, and emerging multi-omic studies, we outline how PBTs exploit physiological immune maturation programs to establish immune evasion, sustain chronic inflammation, and promote therapy resistance. We further discuss emerging multimodal immunotherapeutic strategies and next-generation CAR T-cell approaches currently under clinical investigation. In addition, we highlight therapeutic avenues such as targeting tumor-associated myeloid populations and key inflammatory regulators that may offer promising opportunities for future clinical translation. We believe this Review will help address current limitations in preclinical models, improve patient stratification and guide rational design of therapeutic strategies.

C.title: NAD+ Attenuates Neuroinflammation in Ischemic Stroke by Suppressing the cGAS- STING Pathway via Mitochondrial Homeostasis Restoration.
C.abstract: Stroke remains one of the leading causes of death and disability worldwide, with neuroinflammation playing a critical role in its pathogenesis. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway is a major driver of innate immune responses activated by endogenous DNA, including mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), and contributes significantly to post-ischemic neuroinflammation. Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), a vital metabolic coenzyme, has demonstrated anti-inflammatory potential in various diseases, including stroke; however, its specific role in regulation of neuroinflammation following stroke remains unclear. In this study, we examined the protective effects of NAD+ against ischemic stroke and explored its role in modulating cGAS-STING-mediated neuroinflammatory responses. Utilizing a transient middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion mouse model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation BV2 microglia model, we observed that NAD+ treatment significantly reduced infarct volume and brain edema, and improved neurological outcomes. NAD+ reduced the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and facilitated the polarization of microglia from pro-inflammatory M1 to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. This effect was associated with the inhibition of cGAS-STING-TBK1 signaling pathway activation. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic knockdown of STING largely abrogated the anti-inflammatory effects of NAD+ in BV2 microglia, indicating a STING-dependent mechanism. Furthermore, NAD+ restored mitochondrial respiratory function and reduced cytoplasmic mtDNA leakage, suggesting that the improvement of mitochondrial homeostasis may underlie the suppression of cGAS-STING-TBK1 signaling pathway by NAD+. Our findings indicate that NAD+ alleviates neuroinflammation following brain ischemia/reperfusion injury by regulating mitochondrial homeostasis and attenuates the cGAS-STING-TBK1 signaling pathway activation in microglia, thereby providing new therapeutic insights for ischemic stroke.

C.title: hnRNPU regulates the sorting of exo-miR-125a-5p in colon epithelial cells and its role in realgar-induced central nervous system toxicity.
C.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Elucidating the mechanisms underlying realgar-induced toxicity is essential for the early prevention and treatment of arsenic-related adverse effects and for reducing the associated healthcare burden.
AIM OF STUDY: Owing to its poor solubility, realgar preferentially accumulates in the intestine after oral administration. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanism by which realgar regulates exosomal miR-125a-5p (exo-miR-125a-5p) sorting in colonic epithelial cells and to investigate the role of exo-miR-125a-5p in realgar-induced central nervous system (CNS) toxicity.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A chronic realgar-exposed mouse model was established and combined with AAV9-mediated hnRNPU knockdown, miR-125a-5p-enriched exosome administration, and probiotic intervention. Complementary in vitro studies were performed using YAMC cells subjected to hnRNPU silencing or co-treatment with realgar and L-cysteine sulfinic acid (LCSA). Small RNA sequencing, 16S rDNA sequencing, quantitative proteomics, untargeted metabolomics, RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), miRNA pull-down, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), Western blotting, and other molecular biological approaches were integrated to systematically investigate the molecular mechanism underlying realgar-regulated exo-miR-125a-5p sorting in colonic epithelial cells and its contribution to realgar-induced CNS toxicity.
RESULTS: Realgar exposure induced dose-dependent colonic injury, altered the exosomal miRNA profile of colonic epithelial cells, and significantly reduced the secretion of exo-miR-125a-5p. Mechanistically, the RNA-binding protein hnRNPU directly bound mature miR-125a-5p, enhanced its post-transcriptional stability, and promoted its nuclear retention, thereby limiting its loading into exosomes. Realgar-induced gut microbiota dysbiosis reduced the abundance of Lactobacillus and the level of its metabolite, LCSA, resulting in aberrant upregulation of hnRNPU. The consequent reduction in circulating exo-miR-125a-5p relieved repression of the STAT1 signaling pathway, leading to activation of the microglial STAT1-NLRP3 inflammasome axis and exacerbation of realgar-induced CNS toxicity.
CONCLUSION: Realgar induces both colonic and central nervous system toxicity. Mechanistically, realgar disrupts gut microbial homeostasis, depleting Lactobacillus-derived LCSA, which promotes hnRNPU expression and enhances the nuclear retention of mature miR-125a-5p. This process suppresses miR-125a-5p sorting into exosomes, reduces circulating exo-miR-125a-5p levels, and consequently activates the microglial STAT1-NLRP3 inflammasome pathway, thereby aggravating CNS toxicity. These findings identify a previously unrecognized gut microbiota-metabolite-RNA-binding protein axis governing exosomal miRNA sorting and establish exo-miR-125a-5p as a critical mediator linking intestinal injury to neuroinflammation. This study provides new mechanistic insights into realgar-induced colonic and CNS toxicity and expands our understanding of gut-brain axis-mediated toxicological mechanisms.

C.title: Outcome and complications of endovascular embolization for vein of Galen malformations: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
C.abstract:
OBJECT: There have been many multidisciplinary approaches to the treatment of vein of Galen malformations. Endovascular embolization is the first option for treatment. However, the effects of the treatment remain controversial. The aim of this study is to assess the efficacy and safety of endovascular embolization to treat patients with vein of Galen malformations.
METHODS: This paper includes a retrospective analysis of a sample of 667 patients who underwent endovascular embolization to treat vein of Galen malformations. The data were obtained through a literature search of PubMed databases. The authors also evaluate the efficacy and safety of the treatment. Mortality within the follow-up period is analyzed. Pooled estimates of proportions with corresponding 95% CIs were calculated using raw (i.e., untransformed) proportions (PRAW).
RESULTS: In the 34 studies evaluated, neonates accounted for 44% of the sample (95% CI 31%-57%; I(2) = 92.5%), infants accounted for 41% (95% CI 30%-51%; I(2) = 83.3%), and children and adults accounted for 12% (95% CI 7%-16%; I(2) = 52.9%). The meta-analysis revealed that complete occlusion was performed in 57% (95% CI 48%-65%; I(2) = 68.2%) of cases, with partial occlusion in 43% (95% CI 34%-51%; I(2) = 70.7%). The pooled proportion of patients showing a good outcome was 68% (95% CI 61%-76%; I(2) = 77.8%), while 31% showed a poor outcome (95% CI 24%-38%; I(2) = 75.6%). The proportional meta-analysis showed that postembolization mortality and complications were reported in 10% (95% CI 8%-12%; I(2) = 42.8%) and 37% (95% CI 29%-45%; I(2) = 79.1%), respectively. Complications included cerebral hemorrhage, cerebral ischemia, hydrocephalus, leg ischemia, and vessel perforation.
CONCLUSIONS: The successful treatment of vein of Galen malformations remains a complex therapeutic challenge. The authors' analysis of clinical history and research literature suggests that vein of Galen malformations treated with endovascular embolization can result in an acceptable mortality rate, complications, and good clinical outcome. Future large-scale, multicenter, randomized trials are necessary to confirm these findings.

C.title: MgSO4 alleviates anxiety-like behaviours in mice after traumatic brain injury by inhibiting astrocytic TRPM7 in the amygdala.
C.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reports indicate anxiety as one of the most prevalent mental modifications that occur following traumatic brain injury (TBI). Transient Receptor Potential Melastatin 7 (TRPM7) is extensively distributed throughout the nervous system. It regulates intracellular homeostasis of calcium and magnesium ions, regulates the functions of glial cells, including astrocytes in the central nervous system, influences the inflammatory cascade, and may play a significant role in anxiety pathogenesis. However, the potential of astrocytic TRPM7 in the treatment of TBI-induced anxiety remains largely unexplored. The magnesium ion (Mg2+) is an essential endogenous neuroprotective agent in the brain. A previous study has demonstrated that magnesium sulphate (MgSO4) can markedly reduce TBI-induced neuroinflammation and possess neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the efficacy of MgSO4 in alleviating anxiety is unclear. Therefore, this study utilised a rodent model of TBI to investigate whether MgSO4 could mitigate anxiety-like behaviours following mild TBI by inhibiting astrocytic TRPM7.
METHODS: Mild TBI was induced in male mice utilising the Feeney weight-drop paradigm with the rapid delivery of 2 μL of MgSO4 (100 mg/kg) into the left lateral ventricle. Behavioural and pathological changes were assessed at various time intervals following injury utilising neurological severity score, the elevated plus-maze (EPM) test, and the open field test (OFT). Molecular and structural modifications were examined using transcriptomic analysis, real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction, local field potential recordings, and immunofluorescence staining.
RESULTS: Our findings revealed that mild TBI led to a diminished percentage of time spent in the central zone during the OFT, a reduced percentage of entries and time spent in the open arm during the EPM test, a decrease in the number of grid crossings, lowered serum Mg2+ levels, and a reduction in θ and γ power and θ-γ phase coupling. Additionally, there was a decrease in the intensity of PSD95 and synaptophysin in the amygdala, a reduction in MAP2 intensity in the amygdala, an increase in GFAP and Iba1 intensity in the amygdala, enhanced cytoskeletal hypertrophy and radial extension of astrocytes, along with heightened colocalization of TRPM7 with GFAP in the amygdala, and enhanced colocalization of IL-1β with GFAP. Notably, MgSO4 administration effectively reversed these pathological and functional deficits.
CONCLUSIONS: MgSO4 mitigates anxiety-like behaviours in mice after mild TBI by inhibiting astrocytic TRPM7 in the amygdala, indicating a potential therapeutic approach for post-TBI anxiety.

C.title: HDAC6 inhibition attenuates early brain injury after experimental subarachnoid hemorrhage and suppresses neuroinflammatory responses.
C.abstract: Early brain injury (EBI) after subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is closely associated with microglia-driven neuroinflammation, yet effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) has been implicated in neuroinflammatory regulation, but its role in microglial inflammatory activation after SAH remains unclear. In the present study, we investigated whether HDAC6 targeting attenuates SAH-induced EBI through modulation of microglia-associated neuroinflammation. A mouse prechiasmatic cistern blood-injection model of SAH and an Hb-stimulated primary microglia model were used to evaluate the effects of compound 13-7, an HDAC6-targeting inhibitor. We found that HDAC6 expression was significantly upregulated after SAH and was predominantly localized in microglia and neurons. Treatment with compound 13-7 increased α-tubulin acetylation in microglia, reduced brain edema, improved neurological deficits, and decreased neuronal apoptosis. In addition, compound 13-7 attenuated microglial inflammatory activation, reduced pro-inflammatory gene expression, decreased brain tissue levels of TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL-6, and increased IL-4, IL-5, and IL-10 levels. In vitro, compound 13-7 protected neurons primarily through modulation of microglia-mediated inflammatory responses rather than by directly acting on neurons. Mechanistically, compound 13-7 reduced the p-P65/P65 ratio and suppressed NF-κB-related inflammatory gene expression in Hb-stimulated microglia. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that HDAC6 targeting attenuates SAH-induced EBI and improves neurological outcomes, at least partly by suppressing microglia-associated neuroinflammation and restoring inflammatory cytokine balance. Inhibition of NF-κB signaling may contribute to the anti-inflammatory effects of compound 13-7, highlighting HDAC6 as a potential therapeutic target for SAH-induced EBI.

C.title: Clazosentan, Endothelin-A Receptor Antagonist, Suppresses Interleukin-6 Expression in Cerebrospinal Fluid after Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
C.abstract: Clazosentan (CLA), an endothelin-A receptor antagonist, is used to prevent cerebral vasospasm (CV) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). Although its efficacy has been demonstrated in large-scale clinical trials, the effects of CLA on cytokine and chemokine profiles in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) after SAH remain unclear. Twenty-two patients with SAH were enrolled. Ten patients received fasudil hydrochloride (FH), a Rho kinase inhibitor, and 12 received CLA. CSF samples were collected on days 1, 3, 5, 7, 10, and 14. Concentrations of interleukin-6 (IL-6), monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), interferon-γ-inducible protein-10 (IP-10), and monokine induced by interferon-γ (MIG) were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. IL-6 levels were significantly suppressed during the acute phase in the CLA group compared with the FH group, whereas MCP-1 levels were upregulated on day 1. The peak expression of IP-10 and MIG was delayed in the CLA group relative to the FH group. A strong correlation between IP-10 and MIG was observed on day 5 in the FH group and on day 7 in the CLA group. CLA suppressed IL-6 expression during the acute phase, which may contribute to delayed upregulation of IP-10 and MIG. Suppression of IL-6 may represent a key mechanism underlying the anti-inflammatory effects of CLA following SAH.

C.title: Extracellular vesicle-associated LMP1 from EBV-positive nasopharyngeal carcinoma induces LIF-mediated immunosuppressive macrophage polarization and impairs anti-tumor immunity.
C.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is characterized by a highly infiltrated yet immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), in which tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) contribute to disease progression. Here, we identify an extracellular vesicle (EV)-mediated LMP1-NF-κB-LIF signaling axis that promotes macrophage reprogramming and immune suppression in NPC. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that EV exposure induces transcriptional remodeling across tumor and immune-cell populations, accompanied by an increased proportion of TAMs within the myeloid compartment. NPC-derived EVs were taken up by macrophages, where EV-associated LMP1 induced NF-κB activation, LIF expression, and polarization toward an immunosuppressive phenotype. Loss- and gain-of-function studies, together with structure-function analyses of the LMP1 CTAR1/CTAR2 domains, further supported the requirement of these CTAR domains for efficient NF-κB activation and LIF induction. Functionally, EV-educated macrophages exhibited impaired phagocytic activity and promoted inhibitory T-cell responses. In zebrafish, 3D spheroid, and mouse xenograft models, EV-educated macrophages promoted NPC growth and vascular dissemination, whereas blockade of LIF signaling with soluble LIFR attenuated these effects. Tumor LIF expression positively correlated with CTLA4 expression. In NPC tissues, LIF expression was preferentially associated with stromal macrophages, and elevated stromal LIF expression was associated with metastasis, advanced nodal disease, and advanced clinical stage. Stromal immune-cell LMP1 expression also correlated with LIF expression and was higher in patients who developed metastasis. Collectively, these findings support an EV-associated LMP1-NF-κB-LIF axis that links EBV-positive NPC cells to macrophage-mediated immune suppression and tumor progression and provide a basis for further investigating this pathway as a potential therapeutic target.

C.title: Fucosylated Chondroitin Sulfate Modulates Microglia-Associated Responses and Reduces Aβ Burden with ERK1/2-Related Signaling Changes.
C.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Fucosylated chondroitin sulfate (FCS) is a sulfated polysaccharide derived from the marine organism Apostichopus japonicus. This study aimed to investigate its neuroprotective potential, specifically focusing on microglial modulation and ERK1/2 signaling, in Alzheimer's disease (AD) models.
METHODS: An integrated in vitro and in vivo approach was employed. In vitro, Aβ42-stimulated BV2 microglia were treated with FCS, and the broad protein kinase C activator TPA was used as a pharmacological perturbation to examine whether the FCS-associated ERK1/2 signaling changes were reversible. Cytokine levels, microglial phenotype markers (CD86, CD206, iNOS, Arg-1), Aβ handling, and MAPK pathway proteins (p-ERK1/2, p38, JNK) were analyzed. In vivo, 5xFAD transgenic mice received intraperitoneal FCS for 28 days. Aβ plaque burden, soluble/insoluble Aβ levels, cognitive performance (Morris water maze, Y-maze), cortical Iba1-positive cell counts, activation state (Iba1+CD86+, Iba1+CD206+), and expression of p-ERK1/2, iNOS, and Arg-1 were assessed.
RESULTS: In vitro, FCS attenuated Aβ42-induced pro-inflammatory responses (reduced IL-6, TNF-α; increased IL-10), modulated phenotype (decreased CD86/iNOS; increased CD206/Arg-1), and increased the cell-associated Aβ fraction while reducing supernatant Aβ. FCS reduced Aβ42-associated ERK1/2 phosphorylation and the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic p-ERK1/2 fluorescence signal ratio, and these changes were partially attenuated by TPA. In vivo, FCS treatment reduced cerebral Aβ burden, improved spatial and working memory, decreased the number and proportion of cortical Iba1+CD86+ microglia, and increased the Iba1+CD206+ subset. Cortical p-ERK1/2/total ERK1/2 and iNOS expression were downregulated, while Arg-1 was upregulated.
CONCLUSION: FCS reduced Aβ-related pathological burden, improved selected behavioral outcomes, and modulated microglia-associated inflammatory and phenotype-related readouts in AD models. These effects were accompanied by ERK1/2-related signaling changes, supporting a pathway-associated interpretation rather than definitive proof of ERK1/2 causality in vivo.

C.title: High-frequency rTMS attenuates cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury and modulates mTOR-related signaling and brain-gut-immune phenotypes in MCAO/R rats.
C.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) may promote neurological recovery after ischemic stroke, but its protective effects after MCAO/R and associations with neurotrophic factors, mTOR-related autophagy markers, systemic inflammation, and gut microbiota phenotypes remain unclear.
METHODS: Cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury was induced by right MCAO/R. Rats were assigned to Sham, MCAO/R, and MCAO/R + high-frequency rTMS groups. rTMS was initiated on postoperative day 3. Neurological and motor functions were assessed behaviorally. Western blotting, immunofluorescence, ELISA, and 16S rRNA sequencing were used to examine related proteins, inflammatory cytokines, and gut microbiota, followed by multivariate and correlation analyses.
RESULTS: High-frequency rTMS improved neurological and motor functions, reduced infarction and histopathological injury, decreased TUNEL positivity, and increased the number of Nissl-positive neurons. It upregulated FGF-2, BDNF, and the p-mTOR (Ser2448)/mTOR ratio, attenuated abnormal changes in Beclin-1, LC3-II/LC3-I, and p62, and reduced serum TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 levels. 16S rRNA sequencing showed altered gut microbiota β-diversity and genus-level composition, with several genera associated with motor or inflammatory indices.
CONCLUSION: High-frequency rTMS alleviated cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury and promoted neurological recovery after MCAO/R, accompanied by enhanced neurotrophic support, improvement in mTOR-related autophagy marker abnormalities, and lower serum pro-inflammatory cytokine levels. Gut microbiota alterations were also observed following rTMS treatment, although their functional significance remains exploratory.

C.title: Evidence for maternal autoantibodies in the pathogenesis of preterm birth.
C.abstract: Preterm birth is associated with breakdown of maternal-fetal tolerance and remains the leading cause of global mortality in young children. However, the role of self-reactive antibodies has been limited to a handful of pathogenic allo- and autoantibodies linked to pregnancy complications. Here we identify a shared autoreactive signature of pregnancy in pregnant sera (n = 2,719) relative to never-pregnant controls (n = 130), using proteome-wide autoantibody profiling. Across eight human pregnancy cohorts, we define autoreactivities associated with preterm birth by comparing preterm (n = 688) and term (n = 1,505) pregnancies. Within the signature, antibodies to IL1 receptor antagonist (IL1RA) induce resorption, inflammation and vascular malperfusion in pregnant mice. IL1RA localizes to placental endothelial adherens junctions, suggesting a role in vascular integrity. These findings identify a term pregnancy humoral immune program and shared changes preceding preterm delivery, including anti-IL1RA, which may have direct pathogenic consequences.

C.title: Orbital lymphaticovenous malformations: Current and future treatments.
C.abstract: Orbital lymphaticovenous malformations consist of abnormal vascular channels lined by endothelial cells with a spectrum from venous to lymphatic characteristics. They may be venous-dominant or lymphatic-dominant. These lesions continue to present management challenges. Total excision or obliteration is not always achievable, recrudescence is common, and interventions carry a risk of damaging normal structures. Patients likely benefit most from a multidisciplinary approach, including both surgical and nonsurgical (e.g., sclerosants and liquid polymers) therapeutic modalities. Targeted biologic therapy would be ideal; nevertheless, this goal is complicated by the heterogeneous venous-lymphatic and stromal characteristics of these lesions. Ideally, antiangiogenic agents targeting both lymphatic and blood vascular endothelial cells will be developed to treat these lesions and reduce their regrowth. Further studies are warranted to enhance our understanding of these orbital lesions with regard to their angiogenic (proliferative) activities and profiles of marker expression, with a goal to produce effective medical therapies.

C.title: Stewart-Bluefarb syndrome: Report of five cases and a review of literature.
C.abstract: Stewart-Bluefarb syndrome is a rare angioproliferative disorder characterised by acroangiodermatitis associated with an underlying arteriovenous shunt. This condition should be differentiated from acroangiodermatitis of Mali classically described in association with chronic venous insufficiency. Patients with Stewart-Bluefarb syndrome typically present with lower leg pigmented macules, papules and plaques that can coalesce to form larger confluent patches of pigmentation. Recognition of Stewart-Bluefarb syndrome may be difficult or delayed as the cutaneous manifestations may resemble a variety of other dermatological conditions. Most commonly, acroangiodermatitis may be confused with Kaposi's sarcoma and the condition is often referred to as 'Pseudo-Kaposi's sarcoma'. Acroangiodermatitis may also resemble or coexist with pigmentation of chronic venous insufficiency. As seen in this report, acroangiodermatitis may also be clinically confused with the 'cavernous' form of a capillary malformation. Here, we describe five patients with Stewart-Bluefarb syndrome. In one female and two male patients the diagnosis was delayed as the acroangiodermatitis closely resembled other conditions. All underlying arterio-venous communications were initially diagnosed on duplex ultrasound and confirmed with magnetic resonance angiography. Four patients were found to have a congenital arterio-venous malformation while one was diagnosed with a post-thrombotic arterio-venous fistula. Management included observation and intervention using a variety of techniques including percutaneous or trans-catheter embolisation, endovenous laser, radiofrequency ablation and foam ultrasound guided sclerotherapy. This case series highlights the challenges involved in the diagnosis and management of Stewart-Bluefarb syndrome. Given the local and systemic sequelae of high flow shunts, correct diagnosis and early detection of the underlying arterio-venous abnormality is crucial in the long-term management of these patients and in preventing the associated complications.

C.title: Iliofemoral Venous Stenosis Complicating Large-Bore Access for Balloon Mitral Valvotomy, Unmasking Incidental May-Thurner Anatomy.
C.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large-bore transvenous access for balloon mitral valvotomy (BMV) can be complicated by unrecognized iliofemoral venous disease, occasionally unmasking a congenital variant.
CASE SUMMARY: A 51-year-old woman with rheumatic mitral stenosis and NYHA functional class III-IV dyspnea, on acenocoumarol for atrial fibrillation, was scheduled for BMV. After right femoral venous access and transseptal puncture, hardware >8-F could not be advanced; venography showed a tight, recoiling right external iliac vein stenosis, not responding to intravenous nitroglycerine, treated with angioplasty and stenting, and BMV was deferred. Computed tomography venogram 14 days later confirmed stent patency and incidentally revealed left common iliac vein compression by the right common iliac artery, consistent with asymptomatic May-Thurner anatomy rather than syndrome. Acenocoumarol was continued after stenting, held 3 days before reattempt, and BMV was then completed successfully via the same route.
DISCUSSION: Comprehensive venous evaluation during difficult large-bore access can uncover clinically silent iliocaval anatomic variants and guide individualized, staged management.

C.title: PAI-1-IL-17 statistical interaction and periventricular white matter hyperintensity severity in sporadic cerebral small vessel disease.
C.abstract: The factors influencing the severity of periventricular white matter hyperintensity (WMH) in cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) are not fully understood. This study investigated the multiplicative interaction between circulating plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1) and interleukin-17 (IL-17) concerning periventricular WMH severity. In this single-center, cross-sectional study, we enrolled 151 patients with sporadic CSVD, selected from 526 consecutively screened inpatients. Serum levels of PAI-1, IL-17, and matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) were quantified using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Regional WMH was graded on magnetic resonance imaging using the Fazekas scale. Multivariable logistic regression was employed to assess the PAI-1-IL-17 interaction for moderate-to-severe periventricular WMH (Fazekas scores 2-3 vs. 0-1), with additional adjustments for MMP-9 and sensitivity analyses. The primary interaction odds ratio (OR) was 1.72 per one-standard-deviation increase in the standardized product term (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.07-2.77; p = 0.026). Adjusting for MMP-9 did not substantially change this estimate. The interaction was not statistically significant in the ordinal periventricular analysis (OR: 1.40; 95% CI: 0.99-1.99; p = 0.061) or the deep-WMH model (OR: 0.83; 95% CI: 0.51-1.37; p = 0.468). While alternative binary models showed positive interaction estimates, resampling analyses indicated limited stability, and additive interaction lacked consistent support. These exploratory findings suggest a multiplicative statistical interaction between PAI-1 and IL-17 for dichotomized periventricular WMH severity. However, they do not establish causality, biological synergy, or clinical biomarker utility. Prospective multicenter validation is essential.

C.title: Neutrophil to Lymphocyte Ratio and Neurological Outcome in Ischemic Stroke at 4.5 to 24 Hours: A Post Hoc Analysis of TRACE-III Trial.
C.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Whether neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR), as a marker of increased inflammatory response, modifies the efficacy and safety of tenecteplase is uncertain in patients 4.5-24 h after stroke onset. We investigated this in the Tenecteplase Reperfusion Therapy in Acute Ischemic Cerebrovascular Events-III (TRACE-III) trial.
METHODS: TRACE-III was a phase 3, multicenter, prospective, open-label, randomized, blinded-endpoint trial that enrolled 516 patients from 58 centers in China between January 2022 and November 2023. Patients had anterior large vessel occlusion and evidence of salvageable brain tissue on perfusion imaging, presented 4.5-24 h after symptom onset, and were randomized 1:1 to intravenous tenecteplase (intervention) or standard medical treatment (control). The primary efficacy and safety outcomes were modified Rankin scale score of 0-1 at 90 days and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage or death, respectively. This post hoc analysis in 513 patients with complete admission NLR data compared outcomes in patients with elevated NLR (> first quartile) and non-elevated NLR (≤ first quartile).
RESULTS: In the elevated NLR group (> 3.0), tenecteplase was associated with increased functional independence (61 [30.2%] vs. 36 [19.6%]; adjusted relative rate [aRR] 1.51; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05-2.17; P = 0.03) compared to standard medical treatment. This benefit was not observed in the non-elevated NLR group (26 [41.9%] vs. 25 [38.5%]; aRR 1.12; 95% CI 0.73-1.73). Safety outcomes did not differ in either the elevated or non-elevated NLR groups.
CONCLUSION: Baseline NLR may provide a potential signal for differential treatment response to intravenous tenecteplase in patients with acute ischemic stroke, although these exploratory findings require further validation in independent studies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: TRACE-III is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05141305.

C.title: Targeting the microbiota-gut-brain axis in Alzheimer's and Parkinson´s disease: recent therapeutic approaches.
C.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) are the most common neurodegenerative disorders with limited disease-modifying treatment options. Evidence suggests that the microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA) plays a role in these diseases by facilitating communication between the gut and the central nervous system. Associations have been found between altered gut microbiota composition and function, impaired barrier integrity, dysregulated metabolite production, and immune activation to neuroinflammation and progressive neurodegeneration.
AREAS COVERED: This review summarizes and critically assesses recent studies from the past year to provide an updated overview of therapeutic strategies targeting the MGBA in both diseases. We discuss dietary interventions, probiotics, postbiotics, microbial metabolites, and approaches targeting gut barrier function. We also highlight strategies such as fecal transplantation, photobiomodulation, and PD-targeted metabolism therapies using butyrate and resistant starch.
EXPERT OPINION: While these interventions have shown promising results in preclinical and early clinical trials, their clinical application is limited by methodological heterogeneity, interindividual variability and a lack of standardized protocols. Successful implementation requires carefully designed clinical trials, particularly longitudinal studies of presymptomatic cohorts, standardized microbiome analyses, and integrated multi-omics approaches to elucidate causal relations and facilitate personalized treatment strategies.

C.title: Immunoglobulin GM (γ marker) allotypes as potential genetic markers of efficacy of lecanemab therapy in Alzheimer's disease.
C.abstract: Lecanemab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that targets amyloid-β (Aβ) aggregates, a pathological hallmark of Alzheimer's disease (AD). In the largest clinical trial of its kind to date, lecanemab slowed cognitive decline by 27% in patients with early-stage AD. Lecanemab has also been shown to reduce cerebral Aβ deposition. Lecanemab expresses the immunoglobulin GM 3 allotype, which is defined by an arginine residue in the CH1 region of the γ1 chain and is potentially immunogenic in individuals who lack this allotype. I hypothesize that anti-GM 3 antibodies, generated either following lecanemab administration or acquired previously through maternal-fetal incompatibility or transfusion of allotype-incompatible blood products, may form immune complexes with the therapeutic antibody. These immune complexes could be cleared by phagocytic cells, including microglia, thereby reducing the availability and efficacy of lecanemab and contributing to therapeutic nonresponsiveness. If validated, GM allotypes could serve as genetic markers for predicting response to lecanemab therapy and may help guide personalized treatment strategies in AD.

C.title: Lymphangiogenesis driven by VEGF-C reshapes tumor immune landscape and enables tumor eradication by viral immunotherapy in mouse melanoma models.
C.abstract: Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor C (VEGF-C), a key lymphangiogenic growth factor, has been implicated in improving responses to cancer immunotherapy. We investigated the impact of VEGF-C on the efficacy of oncolytic virotherapy with avian paramyxoviruses APMV-1 (NDV) and APMV-4. Treatment of B16F10 tumors lacking VEGF-C delays tumor growth, and complete responses (CRs) are rare. In contrast, virotherapy of VEGF-C-expressing tumors leads to CRs in most mice. Rechallenged mice remain tumor- and metastasis-free for over two years, indicating durable immunity. VEGF-C-induced lymphangiogenesis correlates with high CD8+ and CD4+ T cell densities near lymphatic vessels. Spectral flow cytometry shows changes in the composition and activation of CD8+ T cells, CD4+ T cells and NK cells associated with CRs, including enrichment of CD8+CD25+PD-1+ effector T cells. T cell composition changes in sentinel and contralateral lymph nodes, indicating a systemic response. These findings demonstrate that VEGF-C-driven remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment enables durable CRs to APMV virotherapy.

C.title: Synthetic host defence peptides modulate phagocytic activity and release of inflammatory mediators by BV-2 microglial cells.
C.abstract: Microglia are the predominant resident innate immune cells of the brain that maintain homeostasis and mitigate damage caused by injury and pathogens. Synthetic variants of host defence peptides, also termed antimicrobial peptides, are designed based on their endogenous counterparts and have been demonstrated to exhibit enhanced immunomodulatory activities, including an ability to selectively modulate the release of cytokines by monocytic cells. These peptides exert therapeutic benefits in a murine brain injury model, but it is unknown whether they can modulate microglial immune responses. We tested the effects of three host defence peptides, namely innate defence regulators (IDR)-1002, IDR-1018 and D-3006, on selected functions of BV-2 murine microglial cells, as well as differentiated HL-60 monocytic cells, which were used as a human model of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) oxidase-dependent reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. It was demonstrated here that IDR-1002, IDR-1018 and D-3006 reduced the production of nitric oxide, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF), ROS, and cytotoxic factors, depending on whether the cells were stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS), interferon (IFN)-γ, or their combination. All three IDRs also reduced LPS-induced phagocytic activity of BV-2 microglia, while IDR-1018 and D-3006 increased this function in unstimulated cells, though our findings are limited to cell lines and require validation in primary or human microglia. By altering selected inflammatory, cytotoxic, and phagocytic readouts of microglial cells in a context-dependent manner, synthetic host defence peptides such as IDRs warrant further investigation as candidate modulators of neuroinflammation, including in animal models of relevant neurological disorders.

C.title: MR-409 promotes neurogenesis and improves neurological function after cerebral ischemia through attenuation of microglial activation.
C.abstract: Neurological recovery during the chronic phase of ischemic stroke (IS) remains a major clinical challenge. Our previous studies showed that the growth hormone-releasing hormone analogue (GHRH-A) MR-409 promotes neurogenesis and improves neurological outcomes. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, a transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) mouse model was used to investigate whether early modulation of microglial activation mediates these effects. MR-409 (2.5, 5, or 10 μg, s.c.) was administered immediately after tMCAO and daily for 3, 7, 14, or 28 days depending on the experimental design. The GHRH receptor antagonist MIA-602 and the microglial inhibitor minocycline (MINO) were used to assess mechanism involvement. We found that MR-409 (10 μg, s.c.) significantly reduced infarct volume and brain edema and improved function and cerebral blood flow at 3 days. It suppressed hippocampal microglial activation and promoted M2 polarization at 3-7 days, decreasing TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 while increasing CD206, Arg-1, and YM1/2, which were reversed by MIA-602. MR-409 enhanced hippocampal neurogenesis, increasing Nestin+, Tbr2+, and DCX+ cells at 7-14 days and newborn neuron survival at 28 days. These effects were enhanced by MINO but abolished by MIA-602. Functionally, MR-409 or MINO improved motor performance at 7 days, whereas only MR-409 improved both motor and cognitive function at 28 days. These findings indicate that MR-409 promotes long-term neurological recovery by attenuating acute microglial activation, improving the post-ischemic microenvironment, and enhancing hippocampal neurogenesis, highlighting its therapeutic potential for IS.

C.title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19.
C.abstract: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartmentalization including immune-specific clusters across DAD patterns. Importantly, spatially informed ligand-receptor interaction analysis revealed intercellular communication signatures defining COVID-19 induced DAD. Transcription factor activity enrichment analysis identified the TGF-β pathway as DAD driver, highlighting the antagonizing roles of SMAD3 and SMAD7 activity during fibrosis. Integration of these data yielded a signaling kinase pathway in peribronchial fibroblasts with amenable novel targets. Finally, spatio-temporal trajectory analysis characterized an alveolar epithelium regeneration program.

C.title: Multimodal data-driven clustering analysis of heart failure patients identifies two distinct patterns of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: Results from the PACIFIC-PRESERVED study.
C.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for over half of heart failure cases but remains poorly defined due to its clinical heterogeneity. In the prospective PACIFIC-Preserved cohort (NCT04189029, n = 155), we applied multimodal deep phenotyping, including high-throughput proteomics, and unsupervised machine learning to identify biologically distinct HFpEF subgroups. Multiview clustering revealed two major HFpEF phenogroups: PEF1, characterized by inflammatory signaling, TNF receptor activation, cardio-skeletal injury, and greater renal dysfunction; and PEF2, marked by endothelial stress and milder perturbations. Conventional diagnostics alone could not reliably distinguish these subgroups, but a multimodal classifier integrating clinical, imaging, and proteomic variables achieved high predictive accuracy (F1-score 0.87). External validation in the MEDIA-DHF cohort (n = 456) confirmed that PEF1 was independently associated with adverse outcomes (adjusted HR 2.27, 95% CI 1.04-4.94). These findings establish a classifier-driven, biologically informed stratification of HFpEF, providing a framework for precision medicine in heart failure.

C.title: Laser treatment in the management of infantile hemangiomas and capillary vascular malformations.
C.abstract: Vascular lesions encountered in dermatology can be divided into vascular malformations and vascular tumors, namely infantile hemangiomas (IH). Vascular malformations can further be subdivided by their flow characteristics and vessel type. Slow, or low-flow lesions are either capillary vascular malformations (CVMs), venous malformations, or lymphatic malformations. Fast, or high-flow lesions include an arterial component, and are categorized as arteriovenous malformations. IH and CVMs are among the most common benign vascular lesions seen and treated in dermatology. CVMs are present at birth and grow as the individual does, whereas IH usually appear days to weeks later and may rapidly enlarge for a period of months to a year before gradually involuting. As the technology has evolved, early and often laser treatment with the pulsed dye 595-nm laser has become our standard therapy of choice. More recently, we have started more patients on combination therapy for IH with the topical beta blocker timolol. If left untreated, CVMs darken and thicken, making them increasingly difficult to successfully treat with lasers. IH involute, sometimes resulting in fibrofatty, atrophic plaques. These individuals can undergo ablative fractional resurfacing with a fractional CO2 laser to improve the texture and appearance of these lesions.

C.title: Electroacupuncture Ameliorating Cerebral I/R-Induced Inflammatory Response through the TLR/TRAF6/NF-κB Pathway.
C.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The inflammatory response plays a crucial role in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury and may offer a new therapeutic approach for stroke. Electroacupuncture has shown potential in treating cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury.
METHODOLOGY: Male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to four groups: the sham group, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) group, sham electroacupuncture (SEA) group, and electroacupuncture (EA) group. The SEA and EA groups received 30 min of treatment after 60 min of ischemia. Body weight was measured before and 24 h after the MCAO/R procedure. Neurological function and infarct volume were assessed 24 h after the MCAO/R procedure. Protein and messenger RNA (mRNA) expression levels of TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB were evaluated using western blot and reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). The mRNA and protein expression of inflammatory markers was assessed using RT-PCR and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).
RESULTS: Compared with the MCAO/R group, the EA group exhibited improved neurological function, reduced infarct volume, and down-regulated expression of TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB. Additionally, in the EA group, the mRNA and protein expression of proinflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β) were decreased, while the expression of the anti-inflammatory cytokine (IL-10) was increased.
CONCLUSIONS: Electroacupuncture exerts a neuroprotective effect on MCAO/R, potentially through the modulation of the TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB pathways. This treatment may reduce the cerebral I/R-induced inflammatory response by influencing the TLR/TRAF/NF-κB signaling pathway.

C.title: Delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol ameliorates oxidative stress, mitochondrial redox state, and neuroinflammation induced by high-fructose diet.
C.abstract: This study investigates the effects of a high-fructose diet (HFD) on brain oxidative stress, mitochondrial redox state, and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, and specifically evaluates whether delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) attenuates these HFD-induced changes. Thirty-two Sprague-Dawley rats were divided into four groups: Control, HFD (10% fructose in drinking water for 12 weeks), THC (1.5 mg/kg daily for the last 4 weeks), and HFD + THC (HFD for 12 weeks with THC co-administration during the final 4 weeks). Biochemical biomarkers (AOPP, DT, KYN, MDA, AGE, T-SH, NADH, FAD, serotonin, insulin) and mRNA expression levels of inflammation-related genes (IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α, NF-κB) were analyzed in brain tissues. The HFD significantly increased levels of protein oxidation (AOPP, DT, KYN, AGE); lipid peroxidation (MDA); and NADH and FAD fluorescence whilst decreasing total thiol (T-SH) content. HFD also increased the mRNA expression of all inflammatory markers examined. In contrast, THC treatment significantly reduced oxidative damage and NADH and FAD fluorescence and reduced the relative mRNA expression of the investigated inflammation-related genes. Strong positive correlations were observed between pro-inflammatory cytokine mRNA expression and oxidative stress markers. HFD causes significant biochemical and molecular damage to the brain. THC administration was associated with a significant attenuation of HFD-induced oxidative stress, mitochondrial redox state, and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, suggesting that it may mitigate diet-associated neurochemical perturbations.

C.title: Modulating neuroinflammation with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists: a scoping review exploring their therapeutic potential in schizophrenia.
C.abstract: Neuroinflammation is a key contributor to the pathophysiology and symptomatology of schizophrenia spectrum disorders. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), clinically approved anti-diabetic and -obesity medication, have been associated with anti-inflammatory properties. It remains unclear whether GLP-1RA treatment can improve neuroinflammation within psychiatric disorders, including schizophrenia. This scoping review synthesizes evidence from clinical and preclinical studies on the anti-inflammatory effects of GLP-1RAs in psychiatric, neurodegenerative and neurological disease models, identifying crucial research gaps and providing future recommendations to guide potential clinical translation. The literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase and PsycINFO and included outcomes of cytokine levels within blood and brain samples. Within the 40 included studies, two were clinical (schizophrenia and alcohol-use disorder) and 38 were preclinical models of psychiatric diseases, Alzheimer's -, Parkinson's Disease, Multiple Sclerosis, Epilepsy and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced neuroinflammation. Preclinical studies showed anti-(neuro)inflammatory effects of GLP-1RAs, whereas the two available clinical studies found no significant changes in peripheral inflammatory markers. As these trials were not primarily designed or powered to test neuroinflammatory effects, the clinical findings remain inconclusive. Differences in study design, inflammatory measurements, pharmacokinetics and dosing may have contributed to the discrepancy between preclinical and clinical findings. Future research should prioritize early-phase dose-finding trials in non-diabetic, or -overweight patients diagnosed with schizophrenia spectrum disorders, evaluating the effects of alternative GLP-1RA regimens on neuroinflammatory markers, safety and clinical symptomatology. This is an essential step to determine their potential mental health-enhancing effects through the modulation of neuroinflammation within schizophrenia spectrum disorders.

C.title: Inflammation-Responsive Baicalin-Delivering Glycocalyx-Mimetic Hydrogel-Functionalized Bioprosthetic Valve for Antithrombosis and Immunomodulation.
C.abstract: Valvular heart disease (VHD), a prevalent age-associated condition associated with high mortality, is primarily treated by prosthetic valve replacement. Bioprosthetic heart valves (BHVs) are increasingly preferred in clinical practice owing to their favorable hemodynamic performance and compatibility with transcatheter delivery. However, current glutaraldehyde crosslinking fails to confer antithrombotic, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory properties, leaving BHVs prone to thrombosis, oxidative stress, inflammation, and calcification, all of which accelerate structural valve deterioration (SVD) and shorten their lifespan. Herein, an inflammation-responsive, glycocalyx-mimetic hydrogel-functionalized BHV (BA@ALG-PP) was constructed using mussel-inspired catechol chemistry, which integrated a vascular glycocalyx-like layer with baicalin-loaded, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive nanoparticles. With the introduction of a biocompatible glycocalyx-mimetic layer on the xenogeneic collagenous matrix, BA@ALG-PP exhibited improved antithrombotic and endothelialization performance, which was further confirmed in vivo by the rabbit intravascular implantation experiment. Moreover, the ROS-responsive nanoparticles effectively scavenged oxidative species and enabled stimulus-responsive on-demand release of anti-inflammatory molecule baicalin, thereby modulating local inflammatory responses. Transcriptional analysis of macrophages indicated that BA@ALG-PP regulated the expression of key inflammatory-related genes (Tnfaip3, Hmox1, Stat1, and Saa3) as well as suppressed pro-inflammatory signaling pathways, including NF-κB, MAPK, and JAK-STAT. Furthermore, BA@ALG-PP demonstrated improved anti-calcification property in the subcutaneous implantation experiments in rats. Collectively, this multifunctional strategy endows BHVs with synergistic antithrombotic, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and anti-calcification capabilities, thereby offering a potential strategy for improving BHV performance that warrants further investigation in large animal models and potentially mitigating factors contributing to SVD. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Glutaraldehyde-crosslinked bioprosthetic heart valves (BHVs) suffer from structural valve deterioration driven by thrombosis, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation, yet current surface engineering strategies remain functionally limited. This study reports an inflammatory-responsive glycocalyx-mimetic hydrogel functionalized BHV (BA@ALG-PP) engineered via mussel-inspired catechol chemistry. The system integrates non-glutaraldehyde crosslinking, ROS-responsive baicalin release, and endothelial glycocalyx mimicry into a multifunctional platform. BA@ALG-PP demonstrates enhanced antithrombotic performance, accelerated endothelialization, effective ROS scavenging, and macrophage polarization from M1 to M2 phenotype through NF-κB, MAPK, and JAK-STAT pathway modulation. Furthermore, it significantly reduces calcification in vivo. This work establishes a comprehensive strategy for BHV crosslinking and surface engineering, offering a clinically translatable strategy to prolong BHV durability and improve patient outcomes.

C.title: ROS-Responsive ECM Mimetic Hyaluronic Acid-PEGDA Hydrogel Enables Palmitoleic Acid-Mediated Suppression of Oxidative Stress and Atherosclerosis via AMPK/NF-κB/NLRP3 Signalling.

These findings indicate that ROS-responsive hydrogel-mediated delivery of palmitoleic acid effectively modulates oxidative and inflammatory signalling pathways relevant to atherosclerosis.

C.title: A myeloid immunosuppressive phenotype defines primary refractoriness to atezolizumab plus bevacizumab in hepatocellular carcinoma.
C.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Despite improved outcomes with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (A+B) in hepatocellular carcinoma, primary refractoriness (PRef), characterised by early progression or short-lived disease stabilisation following treatment, remains a significant challenge.
METHODS: We analysed 1,296 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma treated with frontline A+B (AB-real) and validated findings in 645 trial participants recruited to IMbrave150 and GO30140. PRef was defined by SITC (Society for the Immunotherapy of Cancer) criteria. We performed a multi-parametric analysis of pre-treatment tumour tissue, including machine learning-based quantification of tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes, imaging mass cytometry and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) to evaluate differences in the tumour microenvironment (TME) of patients with PRef vs. responders. Two independent cohorts were further used to refine the TME characterisation through single-cell RNA-seq (n = 20) and imaging mass cytometry (n = 16). We employed conditional inference tree analyses to provide a hierarchical organisation of PRef determinants.
RESULTS: Among 677 AB-real patients and 378 trial participants evaluable by SITC criteria, PRef was associated with inferior median overall survival compared to response (AB-real: 7.3 vs. 31.5 months, p <0.001; Trials: 10.8 vs. not reached, p <0.001). Patients with PRef exhibited higher baseline systemic inflammation (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio [NLR] ≥3), a distinctly immunosuppressive TME enriched in CD163+ tumour-associated macrophages and vascular cancer-associated fibroblasts, a higher Treg/Teff cell ratio, and pro-tumour supportive cellular interactions. RNA-seq of tumour tissue confirmed lower intrinsic immunogenicity in PRef samples with elevated myeloid infiltration. Conditional inference tree analysis identified IFN-γ signature downregulation combined with NLR ≥3 as the strongest contributor of PRef.
CONCLUSIONS: PRef to A+B identifies a distinct biological entity characterised by unopposed systemic inflammation, myeloid infiltration, and T-cell depletion. Targeting myeloid-mediated immunosuppression, particularly in patients with low IFN-γ signature expression and elevated NLR might enhance responsiveness to A+B.
IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab represents the standard first-line treatment for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma, yet the biological basis of early treatment failure remains poorly understood. In this multi-cohort translational study, we show that approximately 40% of patients exhibit primary refractoriness according to SITC criteria - clinically validated here for the first time in hepatocellular carcinoma - and identify a distinct immuno-molecular profile of primary refractory tumours characterised by IFN-γ pathway repression, unfavourable myeloid polarisation, and a distinct spatial immune architecture. These findings provide a biological framework that may inform the design of biomarker-stratified trials and rational combination strategies to overcome primary resistance to first-line immunotherapy.

C.title: RUNX1 in liver graft ischemia-reperfusion injury: a cell-specific framework for ex vivo intervention.
C.abstract: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI) remains a major obstacle to the use of marginal donor livers. RUNX1 has not yet been established as a causal regulator of acute HIRI, and several transcription factors have stronger disease-specific evidence. We therefore asked whether existing human transplant datasets could help define where a RUNX1 hypothesis is most plausible. In 80 paired pre- and post-reperfusion biopsies from 40 recipients (GSE151648), RUNX1 increased after reperfusion (log2 fold change 1.449; FDR 1.65e-28), although the between-group difference in within-patient change was not significant for the biopsy-defined IRI-positive and IRI-negative groups. In the single-transplant GSE171539 dataset, RUNX1-high myeloid cells increased from 10.5% before procurement and 10.1% at the end of preservation to 32.9% at 2 h after reperfusion, with the signal concentrated in inflammatory monocyte and Kupffer/macrophage-like states. These observations support prioritizing the myeloid compartment for direct testing but do not establish causality. We outline distinct working hypotheses for myeloid cells, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs), and hepatocytes, and argue that transient pharmacological or targeted RNA perturbation is better suited to the acute reperfusion window than durable viral expression. Translation will require a staged path from causal models to discarded-human-liver perfusion and, ultimately, transplantation after ex vivo treatment.
